“the steering of this universe belongs to Al’lah

(glory to Him)

, and all beings belong to Him and move only by His Leave. He is the Only Being Alive Who can provide life; He is the Director, for He alone is the Creator, the Source of life, and is responsible for the movement of each atom in the universe. He supplies and is supplied by nobody, for He is One and Self-Supporting. If Al’lah afflicts you with misfortune, no one can remove it but Him, and if He wants to bestow favor on you, no one can withhold His Bounty. This occurs in proportion to what you deserve. Oh people! You yourselves have shaped these gods which you worship with your own hands. Do you worship what you have crafted? Woe to you! Do you not realize? Can you not see that they are unable to save you, or even to save themselves from evil? What has come over you that you cannot judge? Oh people! Why do you shun the Creator of heaven and earth, and obey that which can neither harm nor help you? This is but a mockery which you and your fathers have invented, although Al’lah has not supported it with power.”

However, their only answer was:

“We do not care at all whether you preach or not. This is but the legacy of the ancients. Surely we shall never be punished.”

61

He (pth) said:

“Oh people! Do not let the lower life tempt you. Do not be seduced by riches and the strength of which you brag. How can you ask “…who is mightier than us?”

Do you not see that He Who created you is Mightier than you? What is this false pride for, then? If you witness that, then what is this ingratitude for?

62

The materialist comfort and abundant luxury which they had gained from commerce veiled them from God. Their lands, which stretched from a point west of the Euphrates to the coast of the Mediterranean, were a central point for the meeting of world trade.

63

They built their capital, which had such wealth that it was called:

“Irama, the many-columned city, whose like has never been created in the land.”

64

The Almighty described their structural works to us, which indicated their great luxury. He says:

“Do you build a wonder of perfect splendor and skill to trifle?…”:

that is, you build wondrous castles, coffeehouses and amusement centers in places of excellent natural beauty, constructing admirable parks and buffets of the highest degree of beauty; do you then use them for pastimes and luxury, only to waste time in them?! Does this actually qualify you for Paradise?

“You raise factories...”:

workshops and storehouses, containing silk and toys; you decorate the shops and the stores,

“...hoping that you may last forever.”

You think that you will live forever and you have forgotten about death. All of that is but an ornament for this transient worldly life, which harms the middle class and the poor. It makes them incline to the present life, which leads inevitably to baseness, misery and stinginess, making people turn away from the performance of good deeds and charity.

“And when you exercise your power, you act like cruel tyrants”

against one another. If you clash over something, you will be on the brink of cruelly killing each other because of your merciless hearts.

“See by Al’lah’s Light, and follow me”:

reflect on what these buildings, these palaces, and this luxury will bring down upon you. They result in envy and depravity in people’s hearts, annoyance in their livelihood and competition in their life.

“See by the Light of He Who has provided for you...”:

turn your spirits towards Him and think of those of His Graces which He grants to you

“...with what you know”:

referring to blessings.

“He has provided you with flocks...”:

sheep,

“...children, and gardens...”:

orchards,

“…and springs.”:

boons and great donation.

65

Thus, when God sends forth an Envoy, he places them in the middle of the world. He does not place them in a place as isolated as Hadramut, where no one passes other than an occasional merchant coming from India or the Far East.

God says:

“Nor does your Provider destroy cities until He has created an Envoy in their capital

(a town of primary importance)

…”

66

As for the Thamoud, historians are nearly unanimous in agreement that their hometown was in the area of Wadi Al-Qura, along the Pilgrimage Road from the cities of Syria to honored Mecca. The Thamoud are mentioned in the cities of Jordan, which were conquered by the Assyrian King Sargon in (715) B.C. The description of its context says that it was near to Mecca and to the north. The Greeks also mentioned it in their books. They located it in Al-Hejr land, although they called it Thamudeni, while they called the land of Al-Hejr Agra.

If the Thamoud lived in this area, then undoubtedly the ‘Ad lived in what is now Syria.

The ‘Ad, and then the Thamoud who came after them, took advantage of an excellent geographical location, which lay at a junction of the trade routes coming from the east and going west. At that time and up until recently, this area was an intersection of three world roads:

-First:

the trading road from Yemen and the Hijaz to Syria and the African cities across the Sinai Desert.

-Second

: the road from the Arabian Gulf to Syria and the African cities across the desert.

-Third

: the road from Fares (Persia) and Al-Rafedain (the Euphrates and the Tigris) to Syria and the west of the Mediterranean.

By virtue of this strategic spot, these people were able to take advantage of the trade traffic. They offered assistance in carrying merchandise, as well as providing security services against thieves. Other services they offered included providing food, drink, and fodder for animals, inns for merchants to rest in, and storehouses for preserving goods. They most likely became world merchants later on.

According to the quoted verses, we can also conclude that the ‘Ad and then the Thamoud had an advanced civilization as regards its structure and culture. The Almighty described them as a discerning people, saying:

“We also destroyed the ‘Ad and the Thamoud. This is vouched for by their ruins. Satan had made their foul deeds seem fair to them, and debarred them from the right path, keen-sighted though they were.”

They were masters in worldly science.

67

It is not strange that these same people were enlightened with scientific and literary cultures. The wonderful constructions and factories which they raised surely required competent engineers, and would not have been possible without a developed science of mathematics, and consequently, high standards in all kinds of education. They were able to attain that scientific knowledge because of their special location. It has been said that

“wherever trade meets, minds are fertilized.”

This Envoy called on his people to worship God and to obey Him, for if they did so, He would send abundant rain upon them from heaven and would add to their strength. The words of our master Hud (pth) are those of a man who knew God’s Rules, because when God sends an Envoy to a nation and they do not follow him, He afflicts them with spiritual and physical distress. He makes them taste of the lightest chastisement before the greatest chastisement, so that they will return to God.

God says:

“We sent forth to other nations before you...”:

We sent Envoys forth to them as We have sent you (oh Mohammad), but they opposed their Envoys. Therefore God smote them with hardship, poverty and disease,

“…and afflicted them with physical adversity and spiritual calamity...”

What is the purpose of this distress? It is

“...so that they may repent and return”:

that is, to make them turn to God and purify their spirits. (These calamities befall you so that you will pray to God and obtain a clear spirit. Hence, affliction is sent because of what is in your spirit. Repent and resort to God. If you resort and draw near to Him, your spirit will be cleansed of the microbe which has caused your neediness, illness and misfortunes. Then God will bless you and will end your suffering).

68

God says:

“Whenever We sent a Prophet to a city, We afflicted its people with physical adversity and spiritual calamity...”:

when the Envoys come, and people do not believe them, the Almighty God puts those people under stress out of His Mercy and Tenderness. Whenever God sent a sign to any nation in the world, calling them to believe that there is no god but Al’lah, and they did not believe this sign, He afflicted them with calamity. The Almighty does not destroy a nation until He has sent His Envoys to them. If they then fail to repent, He sends them distress in the form of both spiritual and physical torment

“…so that they may repent…”

This torture and stress show that there is the potential for repentance. The purpose is only to make people invoke God, so that their spirits will be cured of what has settled in them.

This is God’s Saying. Those who say that God creates some people for Paradise and others for Hell are mistaken in their view, for such an idea is in contradiction of the Godly Justice.

The Almighty tells us that when people resist their Envoy, He puts them under stress so that they may return to Him. In that act of returning, the wickedness leaves their spirits and they become pure. God’s Call addresses all of humanity.

“Then...”,

when they insisted on shunning Him and did not repent,

“…We changed adversity to good fortune...”

When the germ came to be so deep-rooted in their spirits that there was no longer any hope of saving them, He gave them all that they desired and allowed them to enjoy this worldly life, so that they might give thanks. (He could have obliged them with such generosity to begin with, but there are only a few people who give thanks, and therefore instead, He begins with affliction). After that, if they did not return to Him, they would be ruined,

“…until they completely forgot...”:

these people did not appreciate the Graces of God. Although they became rich and had an abundantly luxurious lifestyle, nonetheless, they did not return to God or pray to Him any more. They forgot everything

“...and said: our fathers were also touched by sorrows and joys...”:

our fathers were also subject to both good and bad circumstances. They did not ascribe their affliction to their own deeds or actions. They believed that it was simply the vagaries of time,

“…but then suddenly, We called them to account while they were heedless.”

During their neglect, destruction was brought down upon them suddenly, without any advance notice.

69

If God had settled His Judgment in Al-Azal and predestined our fates, as some claim, then what is the purpose of the Envoys and the disasters? We can see from this that what they say is completely wrong. There is a way to return, and we do have the ability to repent. The Almighty has sent us Envoys and leaders, and He has granted you the power of thought and has revealed the whole universe to your eyes so that you may be reminded. If you use your ability to think and are guided, He will bestow good things on you and will not exert pressure on you.

Indeed, that is what happened to the ‘Ad. God sent them only the lightest chastisement. He held back the rain, damaging their orchards and livestock; consequently, their economy and infrastructure collapsed. Our master Hud (pth) explained the reasons to them. He said:

“My people, seek the Forgiveness of your Provider…”:

believe in Him. If you think about anything, you will be guided. Who raised you up when you were just a drop of semen inside the belly of your mother? Everything indicates the Provider. If you do not seek forgiveness in order to be cured of these lowly yearnings, then they will continue to cling to your heart. Adultery, stealing and killing are crimes that occur in the spirit. If you seek forgiveness, repent and render good deeds, you will draw nearer to God, and your spirit will be cured. At that time, you would accompany God’s Envoy (cpth), and through being in his company you would understand both virtue and vice. In this way, you would praise God, Who has protected you from committing wrongs and has showed you their reality,

“…and turn to Him in repentance…”:

turn from your present actions.

“He will send abundant rain upon you from heaven…”:

they were suffering distress and hardship.

“He will add strength to yours. Do not turn away from Him, for you are wrongdoers.”:

you have deprived yourselves of blessings. None of your advantages are real or permanent. You live only so that you can be the possessor of perfection and favor. You were created to be charitable.

70

For this reason, we find that all people see the Envoys to be evil omens, for when they do not respond to them, God afflicts them with many kinds of torture.

The Almighty God sent the lightest torment before the greatest torment to the ‘Ad, but they neither surrendered nor returned. Moreover, they said to him (pth):

“such speech as yours is not proof enough to make us forsake our gods and worship a single god. What you say is nothing other than fancies that are in conflict with our reality and our experience. Why should we not be proud of our life, our factories and our palaces, which are symbols of advancement and progress, and which distinguish us from all other backward nations? Shall we turn from that to devotion, and follow methods to believe in what is hidden? This thing which you deem to be corruption, we regard as goodness and progress.”

God says:

“When it was said to them: ‘do not commit evil in the land’, they replied: ‘we do nothing but good.’ However, they were evil-doers, though they did not perceive it.”

71

They said:

“we can only suppose that our gods have afflicted you with evil since you deny their divinity, and therefore they have hidden the truth from you, making you say these words. We advise you to quit this superstition and turn to worship what your fathers used to worship.”

However, our master Hud (pth) answered them:

“Al’lah is my witness, and so are you, that I am done with what you serve other than Him…”

Thus he (pth) overwhelmed them with his argument and challenged them all.

“…scheme against me and give me no respite. I have put my trust in Al’lah, my Provider and yours. There is no living creature outside His control. Straight is the path of my Provider.”

They could hatch whatever plans they wanted; he (pth) was brave and sure of himself because he was following the right path without error, and had surrendered to God. The Almighty God crippled their power, and made cowardice and terror flow into the depths of their hearts. In this way, they bowed their heads humbly before his majestic greatness. The Almighty clothed him in a garment of divine Grandeur because he was His Envoy.

72

When he warned them of the consequences of their actions, they said:

“…we do not care at all whether you preach or not.”:

this is our path and our creed. We do not care,

“This is but the legacy of the ancients.”:

this is the way that was followed by our forefathers. Why do you want to change the creed that we have inherited from them?

“Surely we shall never be tortured.”:

your admonition is baseless.

73

Thus, the ‘Ad did not accept the call of their Envoy (pth) and they persisted in their love of the earthly life. Furthermore, they asked our master Hud (pth) to bring down his threats upon them if he was really telling the truth.

God says:

“Tell of the ‘Ad’s compatriot, who warned his people with annihilation, and there have been other Envoys before and since his time, saying: ‘serve none but Al’lah, I fear for your momentous day of torment.’ They replied: ‘have you come to turn us away from our own gods? Bring down your threats upon us if what you say is true!’ He said: ‘only Al’lah knows when it will come. I declare to you the words for which I was sent. However, I can see that you are ignorant.’ Thereafter, when they saw a cloud heading for their valleys, they said: ‘here is a passing cloud that will bring us rain.’ Not at all! It is that which you have sought to hasten: a hurricane bringing a woeful scourge. It will destroy everything at the bidding of its Provider. When the morning came there was nothing to be seen except their ruined dwellings. Thus We reward the wrongdoers. We had given them great power….”:

they were the masters of the world,

“…and We may give the same to you; We granted them ears and eyes and hearts…”:

they had made great progress in the worldly sciences,

“…yet their ears, their eyes, their hearts were of no avail since they denied the Signs of Al’lah. The scourge at which they scoffed was fair for them.”

74

The People of Our Master Sa’leh (Peace is through him)

The People of Thamoud

Al’lah, the Almighty, sent the people of Thamoud their brother Sa’leh. He says:

“To the Thamoud We sent their compatriot Sa’leh. He said: ‘worship Al’lah, my people; you have no god but Him. It was He Who made you from the earth and gave you dwellings upon it. Seek forgiveness from Him and turn to Him in repentance. Indeed my Provider is Near at hand and Responsive’.”

75

Indeed, the Envoys’ mission is the same in every time and place. It is to invite people to Al’lah, acquainting them with His Perfection and demonstrating the wisdom behind His Orders and Prohibitions. This is because if people know their Provider scientifically, they will understand everything. If, however, they lead themselves astray from the Provider, they will find no defender and will live in darkness, for deception will blind them from witnessing reality. Thus, they will see nothing but the appearance of things.

In this way, unbelievers look at the truth in reverse. When their Envoy addresses them from the correct standpoint, they deny their mission and disdain their behavior. This happens because, according to their incorrect thinking, this Envoy addresses them in a way that contravenes their perceptions and acts in a way that is flooded with purity, honor and sacrifice. This contradicts the validity of the impurities in which they take pleasure.

Hence, it is no wonder that the blind of heart feel darkness in the summery midday, and dispute the truth even after it has come to light.

In this way, the people of Thamoud denounced their Envoy’s call to return to Al’lah and showed astonishment at his invitation.

Al’lah says of them:

“They said: ‘oh, Sa’leh! We placed great hopes in you before this’…”:

we considered you wise.

“…would you now forbid us to serve the gods that our fathers worshipped?”:

would you bring us a new religion?! All those who preceded us followed the same way! Have you alone brought us a new thing?! Will you dissent from all those who went before us?!

“…truly, we strongly doubt the faith to which you call us.”:

the aberrance of this is clear and obvious.

76

Similarly, the people of Midian displayed such a denial when

“They said: oh, Sho’aib! Do your prayers teach you that we should renounce the gods of our fathers?”:

“we have followed this way throughout our whole lives. Are you alone the judicious one amongst us now? All people adopted this way and were worshipping idols.” “…should we not do as we please with our money?”:

“are we not free to deal with our money as we please? Do you interrupt our free spending of our own wealth?” “Truly, we deemed you forbearing and wise.”:

as they had praised him greatly before, they now said to him:

“does your mind guide you to this now? Is this logical speech?”

77

Such a thing may happen nowadays, for you may clarify the disadvantages of the present civilization for people, and illustrate how it has become a cause of unhappiness and pain. These feelings spring from the very same source which people mistake for happiness

-

so much so that they substitute it for the religion of God, their Creator and Provider.

If you clarify this, they will denounce you and deride you, throwing the same accusations at you that were brought against others before you. As God says:

“When it is said to them: ‘do not corrupt people in the land’…”:

if you advise them not to corrupt people with buildings, ornamentation, luxury and amusement centers, they will answer you:

“these are Al’lah’s Graces; would you have us regress into the past? They had no civilization in the past.” “…they reply: ‘we do nothing but good’.”:

“through these amusements we do nothing more than entertain ourselves.” “However, they are the corrupters, though they may not perceive it.”:

they think that they are doing good.

“When it is said to them: ‘Believe as others believe’…”:

if they are told to consider those who went before them, and think of their deeds,

“…they reply: ‘Are we to believe as fools believe?’ “:

“those people were ignorant, they had no civilization. Were we created only to work?! We must have good times.” “Truly, it is they who are the fools, if they but knew.”:

what will afflict them.

78

Like the ‘Ad, the people of Thamoud had an advanced civilization, the main defining characteristic of which was building; hence, the Almighty called them

“…owners of stones…”

79

80

Moreover, the great wealth they obtained through trade and an excellent, strategic location on the commercial road helped them to build up their civilization. They exploited that money in raising

81

the earth and making gardens irrigated by fountains, amidst which they built towering palaces.

82

As well as this, they cut houses out of the mountains in which they passed the summer in comfort. The Almighty says, through the words of our master Sa’leh (pth):

“Are you to be left safe in this land.”

thinking that you shall remain here forever?! Do you think that there is no God steering this universe, who controls you? Do you feel safe from death?

“Amidst gardens of fountains.”:

will you stay here? Think about those who preceded you. They have died and are now under the earth.

“Cornfields and palm-trees laden with edible fruit.”:

their fruit are consistent and suspended in the air;

“…edible fruit”

can be easily digested. Is it only to be eaten?

“Hewing your dwellings in the mountains…”:

you cut blocks out of the mountains to build huge, well-arranged, neat palaces,

“…leading a luxurious life?”:

is this a comfortable and pleasant life! (How frequently the Almighty illustrates and warns against building high towers because of the significant danger they pose to people!).

“Have fear of Al’lah and follow me. Do not perform the bidding of transgressors,”

those whose spirits became extravagant,

“who corrupt in the earth and reform nothing,”

83

inciting and spreading corruption amongst people through their deeds.

We can say that the Thamoud were a substitute for the ‘Ad with their civilization which followed the same pattern, but they did not surpass them in either power or science.

If we return to the aforementioned verses, scrutinizing them anew, we will see that Sa’leh (pth) cautioned them about their civilization, revealing its corrupting effect and the unhappiness it would bring them, just as it had caused misery followed by destruction to the ‘Ad before them.

Intuitively, the people of luxury condemned our master Sa’leh’s mission and charged him with different accusations, because most people do not believe that there is any way to achieve happiness other than through monetary luxury; or at least, they think that money is one of the most important ways to happiness.

As for the Envoys whose hearts can see the reality of things, they perceive monetary welfare in a way contrary to the people with luxurious lifestyles. While those who live in luxury regard the world through a reversed perspective, the Envoys see by the Light of Al’lah and therefore see what others cannot. The Envoys perceive the truth about deceptive appearances, for the external shapes are false.

Due to the contrast between these two concepts and perspectives, disagreement arises between the Envoys and their adherents on one side, and the affluent people and their followers on the other. Luxury causes class differentiation, division, and hostility between rich and poor; it is obvious that the same luxury also leads the class of opulence to deny the mission of the Envoys, and consequently to be ruined.

Now we want to clarify how corruption is engendered, along with the consequent wretchedness that people mistake for happiness. People remain satisfied with their standard of living when they find that the rest of their society lives at approximately the same standard of living. This satisfaction lasts as long as they do not see anyone overtaking them by too much in this field. For example, people will deem their houses to be lovely as long as there is not a towering palace right beside them. Likewise, they will remain happy with their clothes and furniture unless they notice a neighbor who has newer clothes and better furniture, which surpass their own in their elegance and fineness of quality. Similarly, people are content with their food, drink, places of amusement, and their customs and traditions, whether good or bad, as long as the world around them is not any different. In that instance, they will look with scorn and contempt upon the things which were previously viewed with approval and contentment. They will then begin to grieve, and distress will pursue them everywhere. They will become bored and discontented with their lives.

Now we wonder: who is responsible for the distress and wretchedness in the spirits of these people? Who has robbed them of the satisfaction and happiness which they had enjoyed beforehand?

Is it not the people of luxury who have corrupted the lives of the great majority of individuals who are not so wealthy? This small, privileged group in every society can corrupt the lives of the majority simply so that they can enjoy the pleasures of this life. Not all people can build palaces and possess the appropriate furniture for this level of living. Even supposing that they could, would the rich then stop at that level? Would they not try hard to create ever more modern fashions in lifestyle, and thereby remain distinguished from other people?

Yes, this race will undoubtedly continue, not only to achieve luxury, but also so that people can boast and be proud of themselves in front of others. God says:

“Know that life in this world is but a sport and a pastime, a show and an empty vaunt among you, a quest for greater riches and more children. It is like the plants that flourish after the rain: the tillers (i.e. the disbelievers) rejoice to see them grow but then they wither and turn yellow, turning into worthless stubble. In the life to come, either a woeful punishment awaits you, or the Forgiveness of Al’lah and His Pleasure. The life of this world is but a vain provision.”

84

This race for welfare or for the opportunity for boasting is endless, because the spirit does not remain glad or content for a long time with something to which it has grown accustomed. Rather, it becomes weary and seeks something new, so that whenever it fulfills one desire, new desires arise to take its place. Consequently, life is sure to end long before its desires are fully gratified; God says:

“Your hearts are taken up with worldly gain until you come to the graveyard.”

85

The spirit’s capacity is endless; it can swallow all the pleasures of existence without being sated and without satisfying its limitless powers. This great ability was prepared by the Almighty for it to be irrigated by His own inexhaustible spring: His Compassion, Omniscience, Majesty and Beauty.

God says in a Holy Saying:

“Neither My earth nor My heaven could bear My Revelations, but the heart of My believing servant can.”

Therefore, if we comply with our spirits and seek to gratify our low desires, we will descend, achieving nothing but a little bit of false, transient pleasure, which will inevitably be followed by wretchedness, boredom, weariness and distress. We might think to find happiness enfolded in them but, in fact, they never relieve us of our misery; rather, they cause us to grow more distressed and aggrieved.

By racing toward such luxury, life grows more complicated instead of simpler, and sadness replaces happiness. The cause behind all this is the wealthy people who are corrupting the lives of the poor with their decoration and adornment, causing the depravity of conscience and principle. They make people become overly concerned with the collection of money so they can achieve their wishes and fulfill their lusts, paying no heed to how they get it, just so they can be like the wealthy and show superiority over the poor. This causes their hearts and lives to become corrupt.

Thus, it is civilization that has caused distress and wretchedness for people, leading to the agonies and grudges that have lodged themselves in their spirits. Besides this, civilization has been able to stir up discord among the different sectors of society, particularly between those who are rich and those who are in need. As the wealthy grow richer and become even more masterful and exploitative, so the deprived become poorer, humbler and more enslaved. Is it any wonder that we find the poor massing themselves against the rich so as to make them drink from the same cup? However, even if these poor people take the place of their masters, they will in time adopt the same mentality, since they have fought for the same aim and have ascended to its peak. Moreover, the great demands of civilization cause people to be stingy to both themselves and their relatives, performing very little in the way of good deeds. Indeed, this matter is considered one of the most important reasons for the sundering of relationships and the breakdown in cordiality between the members of society.

Whatever the case may be, the moral and spiritual crisis in each civilization will not be solved except by getting rid of their material goals. This means returning to God’s Law and obeying His Orders, for His is the only statute that can deliver us from wretchedness in both abodes, just as it saved the honorable companions of the Envoy and their followers. Through the words of His Envoys, the Great and the Almighty has warned us not to become engrossed with the present life to the extent that it absorbs all our capabilities. In this way, we can avoid losing access to eternal life. He has ordered us to walk at its edges rather than to dive into its depths, for by sinking into it, as we have seen and suffered in this age, we will cause corruption in the land. Indeed, when a thing spoils, it does more harm than good; or we can say that it no longer serves or profits anyone.

God says,

“walk about its regions and eat of His Provision. To Him all will return at the Resurrection.”

86

The corruption caused by civilization is not limited to the state of our livelihood and morality. It also causes us to lose our way on the path to eternal happiness, and to lose sight of the purpose for which Al’lah created us. Consequently, our master Sa’leh (pth) warned his people about the consequences of their deeds, revealing the vanity of their beliefs and the evil that lies therein. Similarly, he cautioned them against the corruption they had caused in the land after it had been purged of evil; however, they answered him as shown in the verse:

“They said: ‘surely you are bewitched’.”:

you imagine fancies and then you speak on this basis. The bliss caused by such things is hidden from you.

“‘You are but a mortal like ourselves; show us a sign if what you say is true’.”

87

They asked him to bring forth a sign which would prove him to be an Envoy of Al’lah. God says:

“‘Your sign,’ he said, ‘is this she-camel. She will have her share of water as you have yours, each drinking on an appointed day. Do not molest her or the scourge of a fateful day will fall upon you.’ But they bereaved her, and then they became regretful.”

88

God sent forth a huge she-camel which shared the water with them; the water was hers to drink on one day, and theirs on the next. However, they could not endure this division of water and so, in order to take complete possession of the water, they separated the she-camel from her young, causing her to be lost. The Almighty had previously smitten them with different kinds of torture before sending them this sign, in the hope that they might repent and return to Him. They still had a chance to reform their degenerate conduct. However, when they foresaw evil from Sa’leh (pth) and his followers, he replied that the evil they had foretold could only come from Al’lah as a result of their depraved deeds, arising from their mistaken infatuation with the present worldly life.

Yes, their Envoy admonished them many times and revealed to them that they were on the wrong course. He showed them the way to happiness, both in this life and the next. Nevertheless, they did not heed his advice, as they had not thought about Al’lah’s Signs. They were too absorbed in the lower life, causing them to be blind of heart. Would they listen to the one who tried to prevent them from gratifying their low whims? They may have thought of this gratification as fat, but it was in fact a deadly poison that led them to wretchedness, sadness and depravation. Hence, when he persisted in exhorting them over a long period of time, they came to regard him as a hindrance that stood between them and their desires. Consequently, the rich people among them wanted to get rid of him, but God was watching. Before they could put their scheme into action, and before their hands could even reach him, God smote them and their followers with a scourge that came from whence they did not know. God forbid any creature should harm His Envoy (pth)!

The People of Our Master Sho’aib (Peace is through him)

The People of Midian

God provides examples for us out of His Sympathy for us, so that we can learn lessons and follow His Exhortations. This is so that those who are disobedient may repent, and so that the wrongdoers may cease committing their crimes. In this way, corruption can vanish from the land and, through this cleansing, people can live and enjoy true happiness without disturbance. The following is another example He has set for us, and is about the reasons that nations are destroyed. It relates to the people of Midian.

God sent forth their brother in humanity Sho’aib to the people of Midian:

“…he said: ‘obey Al’lah, my people, for you have no god but He. A veritable sign has come to you from your Provider. Give just weight and measure and do not defraud others of what they possess. Do not corrupt the land after it has been purged of evil; that is best for you if you are true believers’.”

98

The folk of our master Sho’aib (pth) were people of Midian, which means, in Arabic, people of this life and those who live in a situation of luxury and excessive enrichment. They set up a wonderful worldly civilization and were commonly known as the ‘Owners of the Thicket’, for they built an earthly heaven which was established on corruption, deceit, cheating and ill-gotten gains. They were people of a high level of urbanization who had a sublime civilization. They attained all of the many pleasures of the present worldly life, and competed in who could enjoy them the most. They also had gardens and orchards, plentiful with fruit with which their Provider had obliged them. However, they deviated and led people astray from His righteous Path, and they sacrificed humane principles for the sake of the lowly life, so that their only interest was in collecting money and withholding it from others. The salesman wanted to ruin the buyer, and the purchaser wanted to rob the seller. This was escalated until they had lost their humanity due to their selfishness, and each one of them had turned into nothing more than a wolf that wished to prey on their fellows. Such a way of life stirs up discord between a person and their brothers and sisters in humanity; it creates hostility, alienation, and hatred among a people, rendering their life an unbearable spiritual hell.

Besides this, when such a person returns to their Provider having left this life, they shall have no good deed in their hands with which to face their Provider and become elevated in His Heavens. Such a person has not been charitable to the beings of God’s creation, but instead oppressed them as much as possible without being deterred. In the end, this oppressor is without the good deeds that would enable them to approach their Provider and gain access to His Paradises. Because of this, they will lose both the present life and the life to come, and then fall down into the valleys of repentance, regret, and diffidence.

For the above-mentioned reasons, fearing for his people out of his love for them, our master Sho’aib (pth) began to admonish them because of the clemency and pity he felt for them. He wanted to save them from the valleys of wretchedness and uplift them to the abode of happiness and bliss. The mission of all Envoys is the same; each person of righteousness who follows them will say the same words:

“…‘obey Al’lah, my people, for you have no god but Him’...”

The people of Midian were afflicted with barrenness, but Al’lah preserved the possessions of our master Sho’aib (pth). He reminded them of the previous nations who had been destroyed because of their love for the present worldly life, and because they indulged in competition within it so extensively.

He warned them of corrupting the land after it had been reformed, by setting up the buildings and palaces which cause corruption in the hearts of people. Behold the outcome for the people of corruption who led the others to do low deeds! Consider their fate…

Our master Sho’aib (pth) spoke to them at length about disobeying Al’lah and playing with weights and measures to cheat others of what was rightfully theirs. He told them that these devilish methods create grudges and hatreds to arise between the buyers and sellers who are engaging in commerce. This deception and wrangling was not only limited to buying and selling, but was included in all transactions in their way of life. This type of behaviour corrupts consciences and gives people the habit of always lying. This surely leads to the spread of corruption across the land, so that wretchedness afflicts people. They will then forfeit their access to the everlasting life for the sake of the impermanent lower worldly life. Therefore, their Envoy admonished them by saying:

“…‘do not corrupt the land after it has been purged of evil; that is best for you if you are true believers’.”

Those who purchase goods from people at a very low price and then sell them essential items at a very high price are like a saw that cuts up wood by moving back and forth; this avails the wood nothing but being cut and torn into pieces. Besides, these actions only lead to hate, dissension and separation instead of cordiality, unity and cooperation.

In fact, buying goods from people at a dishonest price and then selling them the essential items they need at a high price can be compared to the actions of a person who eats but never feeds anyone else; in other words, they are the actions of person who defrauds:

“…who, when others measure for them, exact in full, but when they measure or weigh for others, defraud them.”

§§§§§

In our research, we have now given a brief account of the life of most of the now-perished nations cited by Al’lah in His Holy Book. We have referred to the most significant deeds they have done and the words with which they opposed their Envoys. We then discussed the civilized standard that was reached by some of these nations, such as the ‘Ad people, and about how these deviating civilizations of various types diverted people’s spirits away from the glorification of Al’lah, instead causing them to turn away from Him. This led to people living difficult lives, as material things are unable to replace the soul. By reviewing the lives of these nations, we have also recognized the regrettable ends to which they came having wronged themselves by gratifying their whims and forgetting the purpose for which they had been created.

Now, fearing that the scourge that smote the peoples of Noah, Hud, Sa’leh, Lot, and Sho’aib (peace is through them) may afflict us, and so that we do not neglect the aim for which we have been created, it is necessary to have a pause, and to clarify the purpose of Al’lah in creating creation.

The Purpose Behind God’s Creation of Creation

Throughout the stages of their life, each person certainly recalls many questions. Since early childhood, when perception and recognition first arose, they would ask about what they see. For instance, when a child views the sky, it may ask:

Why do these stars shine?

Where does the sun go to at night?

Where do the clouds come from?

…along with many other questions...

Inspirations and Inquiries

The more this child’s realization grows, the more the questions increase through which it seeks to be aware of this universe. This continues until the child’s inquiries exceed the limits of the material universe, and the child shifts to another field when it asks about the Creator of this universe… Where is He? What could His Aim behind creating it be? As inquisitiveness is part of the principal nature of the human mind, what is the reality of these questions? What is their source? Perhaps they seem to arise out of the very spirit of this child. However, the truth is something different, for all of these questions come from Al’lah, and are addressed to this child by angels through a hidden sound that is emitted in the depths of this young spirit, so as to incite and drive this person to investigate the aim for which they were created.

What is the purpose for which humankind was created? Is this question really unanswerable? Were we only founded in order to enjoy food, drink, and matrimony, or to fulfill other lusts?!

Surely this is not the reason you were created or the aim of your life, because all the creatures and animals that are inferior to you achieve these aims. Moreover, they surpass you in attaining these aims and enjoying such yearnings. If the purpose of our existence is thought to be the enjoyement of eating and drinking, we say that a cow, for example, may gormandize many pounds of its food pleasantly and lustily, so no matter what a person tries to eat, can they exceed the cow in this endeavour?!

Had matrimony been our purpose, we would say that birds exceed humans in this regard by far, when any cock can have many hens, possibly reaching tens in number. In addition, birds have plumage and feathers of unequaled beauty. For example, the peacock has been given such a marvelous aspect that it would have no need of the sciences of humankind and their textile factories and man-made clothes, despite all their complexities and the urbanity of civilization.

Had this been our aim, Al’lah would also have created the human race to be carefree, like the charming and wonderful birds which make no effort, and people would not drive themselves to fatigue, but would ignore the burdens of this tiring and complex life. Besides, He would have provided for humans in a similar way to those lofty and beautiful birds, which attract people’s minds and hearts, and who go out, hungry, in the early morning, and then return at night, fully satisfied, without making any effort or carrying out any wearisome work.

What, then, can be the purpose for which we came to this lower life?

It was said that Al’lah created us to worship Him. The evidence is His Saying

“I never created the Jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

105

Why were we created?!

That is correct, yet this answer in itself is considered to be a question by some people, for you may wonder: why, then, did Al’lah create us and order us to worship Him?

Is it because He is God Who should have His creation (ibad) to serve Him?! Does the Almighty need our adoration, although He is the Self-Existent Who provides for everyone without being provided for by anyone?! Has He created us and commanded us to worship Him only to make us taste all sorts of difficulties because of the orders we must follow and the acts that are forbidden to us?!

Surely, the purpose was none of these, but must be far loftier than this, because the Perfection and Supreme Attributes of God are incongruous with such targets. He does not need us; nor does He need our worship. He continues by saying:

“I demand no livelihood of them, nor do I ask that they should feed Me.”

106

In the Noble Holy saying, Al’lah says:

“Oh, My creation

(ibad)

! Had the first, the last, the Jinn, and the humans of you stood up on one level, asking Me for alms, and had I given everyone what they demanded, that would not have decreased what I have, except to the same degree that the sea may have a lack when a sewing needle enters it.”

107

The purpose of creating us

Thus, God’s Aim behind bringing creatures into being is that people may become acquainted with their Maker, and render good and charitable deeds out of their belief in God and His Envoy.

People can obtain insight and thereby differentiate between goodness and evil, and thereby offer up good actions. Following this course will allow a person to live happily in this life, and after their death they will meet their Provider with a white face by virtue of the beneficent deeds they have offered to His creation. Consequently, they will dwell in eternal delight in His Paradises.

Here is an explanation of what I have previously introduced:

All’ah was in existence, and nothing was in existence with Him. There were no jinns, no humans, no animals or birds, no earth, no sky, no sun, no moon, no stars and no other creature. Whatever you say, He is First and First, and His Existence has no beginning. Nothing came before Him.

“He is the First and the Last, the Explicit and the Implicit, and He is Omniscient of everything.”

108

The purpose of our creation

Being the Origin of generosity, charity, compassion, favor, tenderness, beauty, grandeur, and majesty, and many other additional Attributes of God that indicate perfection, God wanted to create beings so that they could taste His Compassion, and so that He could overwhelm them with floods of His Benevolence and Charity. You could say that God wanted to create beings to overwhelm them with His Supreme Spirit so that they could enjoy witnessing His Beauty and be absorbed in witnessing His Perfection.

The Holy Saying about God states:

“I was a hidden treasure; then I liked to be known, so I created creation and acquainted it with Me; they knew Me through Me.”

Detailing the meaning of this Holy Saying, we say:

“the treasure”:

is the Grand Godly Beauty and the Excellent Perfection.

“hidden”:

not known to anyone.

“I liked to be known”:

refers to the generosity and kindness of the Almighty God, because it is universally acknowledged that the generous show their generosity and kindness, and let their benevolence and charity flow.

“I created creation”:

for it to enjoy viewing the Godly Beauty and to sink into witnessing of that endless Perfection. It indicates that God created creation in that world called ‘Al-Azal’, the prematerial world.

“acquainted it with Me”:

“by creating all beings, I showed them My Grandeur and My Benevolence to them.”

“they knew Me through Me”:

“by seeing themselves they reached knowledge of Me. They then enjoyed viewing that glorious treasure as they saw a part of My Beauty and Perfection.”

All of that had already taken place before we came into this world.

The cause of coming to this world is: if creatures remained at a single degree of witnessing the Godly Beauty and Majesty, they would later feel bored with their state, however high it might be. To receive complete kindness and enjoyment, they had to be elevated in their witnessing from one degree to a higher one that had complete and infinte freshness.

To clarify this, we say: if a person sits in a very beautiful orchard and stays there for a long time, they will undoubtedly become bored with it, and will no longer see its beauty or partake in any enjoyment. To have their pleasure continue, they should move to a new orchard that is more beautiful than the previous one.

Boredom

Certainly, boredom creeps into our spirits for they, in nature, feel weary of constantly being in the same state. They feel bored with the repetition and constancy of even the joyful sounds and tones that we hear, and of the tasty foods we eat, and of all our other desires which do not change. The creature can not soar from one state to a higher one in watching the Godly Beauty unless it has done good deeds which make it sure that its Creator is satisfied with it. Such deeds will be like an elevator through which this creature gets nearer to God. Therefore, the Almighty granted us freedom of choice in order that we can attain much. He has brought us into this world to get the power of discernment that will enable us to distinguish between virtue and vice, insignificant matters and significant ones, low deeds and lofty humanist ones, permanent things and vain, passing ones. Because of attaining this ability, we will rush to perform good actions. For this purpose, the Almighty sent Envoys and Prophets to lead us to the right path.

After reaching this level, we will surrender to His Commands which are of vital interest to us. By seeing the Almighty God and by means of His Light, the benefits of our acts will last forever and ever, both in this life and in the life to come. We will help His creation (ibad) whom He loves as He loves us, because He is the One Who brought them into being, Who formed them, and Who provided for them.

He will be well pleased with us because of our good deeds towards them. When we will return to Him after death, we will be white-faced because of our agreeable works, so that we will approach Him and will enjoy His everlasting Paradises, endlessly rising from one to another that is higher than the previous one. We will rely on our confidence in the high deeds that we have rendered. Those deeds will be repeated before us in the other abode, to act as an elevator for our ascension in the Gardens.

Thus, Almighty Al’lah created humankind to carry out the favours and charity on which the boons and the Heavens in the other abode depend. That is the aim of our existence. If we believe in Him, the Almighty, and know Him, we will be illuminated by His Light, for He is the Light of the heavens and the earth; then we will see what is good and perform it, in the same way that we will see what is evil and will avoid it. He is the Granter and the Creator of every kindness, blessing and charity. This worldly life is of no permanence and all that is on it is evanescent. Only the Face of your Lord will abide forever, with His Manifestation and Donation.

Since people on this earth nowadays have neglected that precious knowledge and have neglected the great deeds which would result from their knowledge of the Almighty God, and since they have concentrated the power of their thought only on this mean, worldly life, woe is expected to befall them at any moment. They are like the previous ruined nations in this respect. However, their woe will be even more calamitous and more doleful.
