In the same way, the spirit of our master Adam (pth) acquired impressions of the Godly Attributes, so that Adam attained knowledge of them all. The noble verse is referring to this when God says:

“He taught Adam all the Names…”:

the Compassionate, the Omniscient, the Omnipotent, the Patient, and all of the other Supreme Attributes of God.

314

These Attributes are the Names which the Almighty God taught to our master Adam (pth). They are the names of the Godly Presence which qualify one for the rank of successor to God on the land. The one who attains knowledge of the Name of God, the Compassionate, is worthy of being God’s successor to His creatures. This is because the Godly Mercy has been printed on his spirit, because of his love for God and his perfect inclination to Him.

The Almighty indicates this when He says, in address to His Envoy, our master Mohammad (cpth):

“Through a morsel of God’s Compassion, you treated them so gently. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would surely have deserted you. Therefore pardon them and implore Al’lah to forgive them. Take counsel with them in the conduct of affairs, and when you are resolved, put your trust in Al’lah. Al’lah loves those that trust Him.”

315

He also says:

“There has now come to you an Envoy of your own, one who grieves at your sinfulness and is solicitous over you, and to true believers, he is clement and merciful.”

316

Out of the compassion which was impressed on the spirit of the Envoy (cpth)

-

which he acquired through his nearness to his Creator

-

he became lenient with all creatures, was kind in how he treated them, was eager to guide them and point them in the right direction, and was clement and gracious with them. These are the qualities which are required by the rank of succession, and they were accomplished in the spirits of both our master Mohammad (cpth) and our master Adam (pth) before him. These qualities were realized in the spirits of every other Envoy, Prophet and leader, to a level proportional to their entry into the Presence of their Creator and their nearness to Him.

Anyone who has not entered into Al’lah’s Presence and who has not had these Godly Attributes impressed on their spirit

-

so that they have not derived compassion, clemency, justice, patience, wisdom, and the other perfect attributes from their Creator

-

is not fit to ascend to such a high position.

God referred to the fulfillment of this quality in the spirits of the noble companions of His Envoy (cpth), saying:

“Mohammad, Al’lah’s Envoy, and those who keep company with him are strict with the unbelievers but merciful to one another…”

317

Turning again to the words about our master Adam (pth), we say: our master Adam (pth) attained knowledge of God’s Attributes and Names

-

such as the Compassionate, the Just, the Clement, the Patient, the Forgiving and the other Names

-

because of the extent to which these qualities were imprinted on his own pure spirit; therefore he was merciful, just, patient and so forth, so that he (pth) deserved to be worthy of the degree he attained.

With regard to what some people think, namely that the Almighty taught our master Adam (pth) the names of pots, utensils, animals, plants and other beings: this is entirely removed from the sublime meaning that is indicated by the noble verse, and does not fit with the context of the verses, which utterly refute this claim. For him to ascend to the rank of the successor of God on His land, and to become a leader and a guide for His creation (ibad), it would not be required for him to be taught, by God, the names of pots and utensils. Rather, what was required was that his heart be colored with kindliness and mercy, and various other perfect qualities.

God ordered Adam to show the angels the Godly Attributes whose stain had colored his spirit, and whose impression had been impressed on his spirit.

Our master Adam (pth) showed these Names to the angels. That is what the noble verse indicates when God says:

“…Then, he displayed them to the angels...”

Then, our master Adam (pth) asked them about the meanings that were folded under God’s Supreme Attributes such as the Omnipotent, the Patient, the Omniscient, and the Commissioner.

God ordered the angels to reveal the knowledge they had about each one of those Attributes. God says:

“…Then, He said: tell Me about the Attributes

(Names)

of these…”:

that is, tell Me the significance and the meanings of the Names that were shown to you by Adam. For example, they were to explain the meaning behind the Names the Sovereign, the All-Powerful, the Subduer, and all the other Names, one after another…

“…if you are truthful”:

in being competent enough to qualify for the succession. However,

“They said: Glory to You…”:

what great Perfection and Grandeur belong to You!

“…We have no science except what You taught us…”:

that is, we have no science other than what You have taught us; we replied according to what we knew by means of entering into Your Presence and according to how truthful we were with You.

“…You are the Omniscient…”:

You know everything about each one of us and about the degree of his knowledge of Your Names,

“…the Wise”:

all Your Actions are within wisdom. You are Wise in Your acts and in Your choices. We do not say this as any kind of objection. We only wish to attain that rank and hope to draw closer to You. You know best who is most fit and most competent for such a high rank. God then ordered our master Adam (pth) to acquaint the angels with the Godly Names:

“He said: Adam, tell them about their Attributes

(Names)

…”

that is, speak about My Supreme Names that they have explained and talked about, or alternatively, tell them about the Attributes you showed them.

“…when he told them about their Attributes…”:

that refers to how Adam (pth) spoke to them in detail about the Godly Attributes that were displayed to them, revealing his scientific knowledge of them and his level of advancement over the angels in that scientific knowledge and its expression. When he spoke about the Perfection of God which is folded behind these Attributes on the basis of his great entrance into the Presence of his Provider, in his speech he surpassed all of the angels so that his greater level of excellence was made apparent. Then their Provider addressed them, as mentioned in the noble verse:

“…He said: didn’t I say to you that I scientifically know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?”:

Adam is higher than you,

“…And I scientifically know what you reveal…”:

what truth you now admit and reveal,

“…as well as what you were hiding”:

by asking for the succession for yourselves.

318

The Hidden

This refers to everything that is unknown to the beings of creation. It refers to hidden things, meaning anything which the beings of creation do not have knowledge of or with which they are not acquainted, whether they are things which have already happened or whether they are things that will happen, and this encompasses anything that God has created or that God will create, be they in the heavens or on the earth. The Almighty God has knowledge of the hidden in both the heavens and on earth because He is the Creator and the Originator. Everything they contain moves through Him and lives through His Sustenance, and their continuity, their existence and their incidence depend on God’s unceasing Supply and Manifestation. He is Omniscient of every spirit and of what it hides. Therefore He knew what degree of knowledge the angels had in their spirits and the function that was suitable for their knowledge, just as He knew the qualifications of the great man, Adam (pth), and his capacities.

As for the beings of creation, they have no knowledge except what they receive from God. They may know nothing of what is hidden in their own spirits or of what degree of science and knowledge they have, just as was the case with the angels when they secretly asked for the succession for themselves. They thought that they had the competence to have that status, knowing nothing of the precedence of our master Adam (pth) or his excellence in that field. Therefore God showed them the truth and revealed to them the degree of their knowledge.

We can understand from the statement

“…as well as what you were hiding”

that is mentioned in God’s statement:

“…I scientifically know what you reveal as well as what you were hiding”

that when the angels said:

“…will You place on it those who will corrupt and shed blood and we glorify with Your Praise and purify for You?”,

their saying was only a spiritual one. That is, they said that secretly to themselves and hid it within themselves. Nonetheless, God was aware of this and answered them in His Address to them. Therefore He made them aware of the knowledge of our master Adam (pth) until their spirits admitted His Wisdom and submitted to His Selection and His Omniscience, surrendering and yielding to Him.

Just as the statement

“…I scientifically know what you reveal…”

shows us God’s knowledge of what the angels revealed in regard to admitting the truth about Adam, surrendering to God, and confessing His Wisdom in His Choice; similarly, the statement

“…as well as what you were hiding”,

that is, of asking the succession for yourselves, shows us His knowledge of what they were hiding and saying to themselves within their spirits.

The Almighty God mentioned these two sayings in order to acquaint us with His Omniscience. There is no difference between His Knowledge of the secret things which a creature hides within itself and the open things which they utter with their tongues. What is secret and what is open are equal to God:

“You have no need to speak aloud, for He has knowledge of all that is secret, and even of what is behind it.”

319

He also says:

“Whether you speak in secret or aloud, He knows what is centered in the chests: shall He Who has created all things not know them all? He is the Most Kind, the All-Knowing.”

320

Having revealed the meaning of the word

“Names”

which means

“Attributes”,

as mentioned in the previous verses, we now have to answer the following question:

Why do we interpret God’s Saying:

“He said: Adam, tell them about their Attributes…”:

to mean that he should tell them about the Attributes of God which Adam had shown them, although the word in the noble verse was

“…their Attributes…”

rather than ‘My Attributes’? We say: we have seen that this story only drives at showing us the sublimity of our master Adam (pth) and his advancement over the noble angels in his knowledge of God’s Attributes. This was what had made him worthy to ascend to the rank of succession. We have also clarified that this purpose implies that the intended meaning of the word

“…Names…”

mentioned in this story is the Godly Attributes. The course of the story clearly and certainly refutes any other meaning.

Therefore the repetition of the word

“…Names…”

in this story certainly means that they are the Godly Names, which are the main subject and the topic of this story. Cconsequently, the words

“…their Names…”

do not mean the angels’ names, but means the Godly Names that were shown to them. To know the names of the angels would not be a reason to grant our master Adam (pth) more sublimity before God; nor would it make him loftier in rank than the angels.

You may say: why do not we interpret the statement

“…when he told them about their attributes…”

to refer to the knowledge that they had about the Names of their Provider?

We say, if we explained the meaning of the verse in such a way, our master Adam (pth) would not then have risen to a standing that surpassed all the angels, because he would only have told them something that they already knew. Consequently, he would not have deserved his succession or risen to a rank higher than that of the angels, since he would not have added any more enlightenment to theirs in relation to the Names that were shown to them. He would have merely been at the same level as any of them. Thus he spoke to them about the Godly Names that were shown to them and eloquently revealed a revelation; thereby he advanced over them all.

Now we must reveal the difference between the words

“…their Names…”

as mentioned in the noble verses and the words ‘My Names’ which are the subject of our discussion. We say, if the address in the noble verse had been ‘tell them about My Names’ instead of

“…tell them about their Names…”,

the meaning would have been completely different, because the statement ‘tell them about My Names’ would mean that Adam should have given them comprehensive knowledge about each Name of His.

As no creature can have comprehensive knowledge of the Name ‘the Compassionate’ or know the degree of God’s Compassion in order to acquaint people with it

-

and so is the case with the Name ‘the Omniscient’ and all of the other Godly Names

-

therefore the verse did not say ‘tell them about My Names’ but

“…tell them about their Names…”

that is, those of their Names which you have displayed to them and which they have explained. This was in order to uncover the degree of Adam’s knowledge of them, and the perfection they contained, according to his nearness to God.

In fact, nobody knows the Attributes of Al’lah except Al’lah the Almighty, and none can have comprehensive knowledge of them because they are without either limit or end. The fact is that a person can only witness the Godly Names to a level proportional to their closeness to Al’lah, the Almighty. A person only acquaints others with a certain degree of knowledge of God’s Mercy, Clemency, Omniscience and other Attributes. Al’lah is Vast and Omniscient.

No matter what degree of knowledge of God’s Attributes you attain, these Attributes are wider than this; whatever rank you reach in that field, your Provider (glory to Him) is higher and more sublime than this. Above all of those who have knowledge there is always one who is more Knowing.

When Adam’s precedence and excellence above the noble angels in his knowledge of God’s Attributes was made apparent to them, God ordered them to enter into His Presence with Adam’s companionship. This was so they would take him to be a shining lamp for their spirits and a leader in their entry into His Presence. Thus He ordered them to prostrate themselves before our master Adam (pth). God says:

“Then We said to the angels: prostrate yourselves before Adam…”

that is, ask to attain science and knowledge by means of him. Bind yourselves up with him in order to enter into My Presence, thereby to view panoramas higher and loftier than yours. Then

“…they prostrated themselves…”:

all of them,

“…except Lucifer…”:

out of his benightedness, because he knew nothing about Al’lah. In Arabic, ‘Lucifer’ means one who mistakes what is right for what is wrong, and that is what had happened with Lucifer. He did not see the reality of the Order, because he knew nothing about Al’lah except that He was the Creator. Lucifer was the one

“…who rejected…”:

the direction to prostrate himself and said that he was greater and better than Adam,

“…and disdained…”:

Adam, and

“…he was one of the disbelievers”:

he did not think of God’s Signs. Had he thought and glorified them, he would have submitted to Adam and acquired a great share of perfection and happiness.

321

You may ask: what is this prostration which the angels were ordered to do by the Almighty? We say: prostration is asking for what you need through spiritual submission and appreciation. To prostrate oneself to God means to ask Him for help and sustenance.

The Almighty God referred to this meaning in many verses of the Holy Qur’an, such as when He says:

“Do you not see how all that is in the heavens and on the earth, including the sun and the moon and the stars, the mountains and the trees, the beasts, the countless oblivious people and many who deserve the scourge: all prostrate themselves before Al’lah…”

322

He also says:

“All who dwell in the heavens and on the earth prostrate themselves before Al’lah willingly or unwillingly; they have their shadows, morning and evening.”

323

In another verse He says:

“The stars and the trees prostrate themselves.”

324

The prostration before God of the sun and the moon and the stars, of the mountains and the trees, of the beasts, and of all those who dwell in the heavens and on the earth: this is nothing but their submission to Him because of their need of Him. They are asking Him to continue to provide them with life, because if this divine Providence goes away from them for so much as the twinkle of an eye, they will disappear from existence and no trace of them will be left behind. For this reason, everything that is contained in the universe prostrates itself to God, continually directing itself toward Him, and continuing to derive Provision from Him.

There is another prostration. This is the prostration to those whose rank and knowledge you glorify so as to get more from them. Through such appreciation and this request for more, you bind yourself to them. If they are believers, through them you will enter the spirit of the Envoy (pth), and gain access to the witnessing of God’s Perfection. This is intercession.

The Reality of Intercession

The nature of the human spirit means that it is predisposed to appreciate the Godly Perfection. However, this appreciation and glorification need the spirit to have an eye with which to see and witness. The physical eye in the human head enables us to see only the things which appear and are illuminated by means of physical lights such as the light of the sun, the moon, electricity, and other means of lighting.

As regards the eye of the heart, that is the heart of the spirit. It sees only by the Light of Al’lah which comes to His Envoy. This light is permanent, everlasting and constantly increasing. The physical lights, on the other hand, are faint and insignificant in comparison with the Light of Al’lah; they are merely a simple beam, a fragment of the light of the Great Creator (glory to His Names). If a spirit was to enter into Al’lah’s Presence in its communication with Him, and became colored with perfection, and acquired this perfection, it would gain this ability and would attain that eye, which

-

when opened

-

would enable it to see and witness this perfection. Then, if this believer was to look around, they would see the people of perfection and notice how they also followed this lofty way; then this believer would love them. The higher the level of perfection above the level of this believer that these people of perfection attain, the more love and passion this believer feels towards them, the more appreciation they inspire, and the more magnificence they have. Since the Envoy (cpth) is superior above all other believers in this field, since he (cpth) is the master of the people of perfection and holds the highest rank, since he is the nearest one to God, you will find that a believer will love God’s Envoy (cpth). This believer will appreciate and revere him due to the perfection with which he was colored, and which he attained from his Provider. For a true believer, there is no creature with a higher position or a loftier rank or with greater prestige than God’s Envoy. When they hear somebody mention the Envoy (cpth), their love will become stirred up in their heart and their spirit will flow to the Envoy with the speed of a flash of lightning (cpth); this spirit will accompany him and be attendant on his noble spirit. However, the states of these lovers are so great that they cannot truly be compared to anything, or said to be resemble anything else.

This believer will proceed gradually in their love for the Envoy (cpth). Their link with him and their communication with God through him will keep rising and ascending. They will continue to advance along the path of appreciation, glorification and reverence until they reach a state when the two spirits have coupled with one another. This will form a bind of appreciation, love and reverence for the Envoy (cpth). This is true intercession. As the spirit of the Envoy (cpth) is always in attendance in God’s Presence, a believer who is coupled with the Envoy qualifies to enter into God’s Presence in the company of the Envoy (cpth). At the moment of entry, by the light of the Envoy (cpth)

-

or you could say, with the one sent by God to be a shining lamp and a mercy for all worlds

-

this believer will see the Light of God, by which they will witness an aspect of Al’lah’s Attributes. They will then passionately love what they see and will fall in prostration before the Presence of God, fully immersed in watching the Godly Attributes. They will witness how Al’lah manifests Himself through the Name ‘the Compassionate’, overwhelming all of creation with His endless Compassion, and through the Name ‘the Clement’, surrounding all of creation with His Clemency. They will view all of the Godly Names, such as the Wise, the Omniscient, the Most High, the Grand, and all of the others, which will make them completely sink into absolute absorption in them, fully surrendering to this merciful and kind Provider. It is their link with the Envoy (cpth) and their communication with God through him (cpth) which will have led them to such great Godly Favor, such high witnessing, and such eternal bliss.

By my life, that is true intercession. It is an intercession of love for and spiritual company with that noble and venerable spirit (cpth).

In Arabic, the word ‘intercession’ means ‘coupling’ and is derived from the word ‘couple.’ This refers to two things which are bound to each other and which remain linked together. The noble verse refers to this spiritual link with the Envoy (cpth) and to this real intercession and binding when God says:

“Al’lah and His angels keep in communication with the Prophet. You who believe, communicate yourselves with Al’lah through him and fully surrender.”

325

Communicate yourselves with Al’lah through him: that is, connect your spirits with the noble spirit of the Envoy (cpth) in order that he will facilitate your ascension into the Godly Presence, because communication with Al’lah is a link between a being and its Provider, and it cannot be accomplished except through the mediator (cpth). God says:

“When you

(Mohammad)

are in them, establish communication

(prayer)

with God for them…”

326

This communication does not only refer to the prayer that is prayed by people moving their body. Correct communication is accomplished when the Envoy is in your spirit and you enter, through his company, into Al’lah’s Presence. This is communication in its reality. The Almighty did not say:

“When you are among them”,

so true communication is performed by intercession with the Envoy, and then the link with God is attained through his companionship.

To perform communication, the Envoy must be in your spirit, because entering God’s Presence is achieved through the company and intercession of the one (cpth) that God sent to return you to Him, the Almighty. Through such intercession between you and him, he (cpth) teaches you how to pray. After he says to you:

“In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful”

he says:

“Praise is to God…”:

oh my brother.

“…the Provider of all worlds.”

This is communication with Al’lah. Then, when he recites God’s Orders to you, you bow, obeying and submitting to the Great God, and prostrate yourself, asking for God’s Help to obey Him. Without this spiritual link and the company of God’s Envoy (cpth), and without communication with God through him, the believer would not have attained this loftiness and ascent; nor would they have attained such sight and witnessing or full surrender to God.

After that spiritual journey in communication, the believer returns having had a brand of Al’lah’s Light illuminated in their spirit. It was lit in their heart by their love for their Creator after what they saw of Al’lah’s Perfection, and what they witnessed of His Sympathy, Tenderness, Clemency, and Mercy for all His creatures. In fact, love is not attained until after this witnessing and viewing. Do you know what benefit is brought by this Godly Light that is illuminated in the heart of the believer?

Through this Light, they will see the reality that is hidden behind the external image. Thus they will not be inveigled by the forms of things, nor will they be deceived by the pictures of people. They will have their discerning eye opened and be able to see by Al’lah’s Light, and thereby this believer will have become a person who can distinguish virtue from vice and truth from falsehood. They will see what is good and know that it is really good, and will therefore like it and incline to it, just as they will see what is evil and know that it is really evil, so loathing, disdaining and renouncing it. That is the sublime degree to which every person should arise, and that is piety

-

seeing by Al’lah’s Light

-

which can be achieved through intercession. This is what God the Almighty urged the believers to obtain when He prompted them.

God says:

“You who believe, see by Al’lah’s Light and believe in His Envoy. He will grant you two portions of His Compassion and make a light for you by which you can go, and He will forgive you. Al’lah is Forgiving and Merciful.”

327

He also says:

“You who believe, if you see by Al’lah’s Light He will give you the power of discrimination and veil your sins from you and forgive you. Al’lah is of great bounty.”

328

Thus, piety is just to see by Al’lah’s Light, and it is a result of your intercession with God’s Envoy (cpth) and your entry into God’s Presence with him. With that, your spirit will become illuminated by Al’lah’s Light, which will protect you from falling into the gulf of error and from carrying out ruinous and evil actions. The person to whom Al’lah has not granted a Light shall find no light.

Intercession, then, is a spiritual state. The Envoy (cpth) who approached his Provider is the greatest and loftiest in making this approach; this is the Envoy upon whom the greatest manifestation and the most shining light and support descend from Al’lah; if he directs his spirit towards those of his companions who come near to him, and who believe in his mission and in what he brought to them from Al’lah, then that Godly Light will flow through the Envoy (cpth) and enter into his companions and those who believe in him.

In this way, the great Envoy will be a mediator between God and His creation, and a means to lighten the intensity of that manifestation in order that the spirit can receive it and bear it; that is the reality of intercession.

God says:

“Those who pray seek the means to approach their Provider, the nearest means. They crave His Mercy and fear His Punishment…”

329

Thus intercession is not for the disobedient or for the people who carry out enormities. If Al’lah, the Almighty, manifests Himself directly to the hearts of people without the mediation of the Envoy (cpth), their spirits will crack and be unable to bear that Godly Manifestation. They will be shocked and will lose their minds because of that light, as happened with those who went to meet God with our master Moses (pth). They were shocked because they did not appreciate him. However, your Provider is Wise, and therefore He chose the Envoys (ptt) who were the most loving to Him from among all people, and who were the most able to bear His Light, so that they could be mediators between Him and His creation (ibad).

Out of God’s Mercy and Tenderness for His creation, He ordered the Envoy (cpth) to direct his noble spirit towards the believers in order to be a means for the Godly Light to flow into their hearts, and to be a mediator between them and their Provider. They then receive purification and forgiveness by means of this Light and regain their spiritual health. God says:

“…and communicate their spirits with God through your spirit, for your communication will give them comfort. Al’lah knows all and hears all.”

330

The prostration of our master Joseph’s father, mother, and brothers is just their glorification and appreciation of Joseph’s knowledge after they had realized his precedence and his excellence over and above them in his knowledge of and belief in Al’lah. Through such admiration and reverence for him, their spirits were bound up with his, entering with him into God’s Presence. That is indicated by the noble verse, wherein God says:

“He raised his parents to the throne while they submitted to him. He said: oh father, this is the interpretation of my old vision; my Provider has fulfilled it…”

331

This meaning is also confirmed in the noble verse which details the submission of the magicians before our master Moses (pth); God says:

“We inspired Moses: now throw down your staff, and thereupon it swallowed up their false device. Thus, the truth prevailed and their actions proved to be in vain. They were defeated and put to shame, and the enchanters prostrated themselves before Moses.”

332

In spite of their high numbers and their mighty tricks, when these magicians were shown what had frustrated their magic by our master Moses (pth), they praised and appreciated his knowledge, and their spirits drew near to him, submitting to his knowledge. Through this spiritual approach to him, and through his pure and chaste spirit, reality was revealed to them clearly and plainly, and no sooner had they submitted than

“They said: we have believed in the Provider of the worlds, the Provider of Moses and Aaron.”

333

When Pharaoh threatened them with punishing torment and crucifiction, they addressed him with the truth their spirits had witnessed, paying no attention to his intimidation:

“They said: obey you we cannot; rather we will obey the signs which we have witnessed and He Who has created us. Therefore do your worst, you can punish us only in this present life. We have put our faith in our Provider so that He may forgive us our sins and the witchcraft you have forced us to practice. Better is the reward of Al’lah and more lasting. He that comes before his Provider laden with sin shall be consigned to Hell, where he shall neither live nor die. But he that comes before Him with true faith and good deeds shall be exalted to the highest rank. He shall abide forever in the heavens under which the rivers flow. Such shall be the recompense of those who purify themselves.”

334

We wonder: how were the magicians able to reveal such a revelation, although they had been brought directly to Pharaoh from different cities, and had not met our master Moses previously or heard any of his guidance before this occasion?! Indeed, praising and appreciating his knowledge made their spirits bind up to his so that they entered into God’s Presence by means of him. Therein, they witnessed reality and said the words that they said, indicating certain faith.

They are, in this respect, like the queen of Sheba (Saba’), who extolled the possessions of our master Solomon (pth) when

“She was bidden to enter the edifice; when she saw it, she thought it was a pool of water and bared her legs. But Solomon said: it is an edifice paved with glass...”

She then despised her own possessions and admired those of our master Solomon (pth), as well as his great prestige. No sooner had she looked at him with a look of admiration than her spirit entered into God’s Presence through his pure chaste spirit. Her tongue translated her spiritual state, for:

“…she said: Provider, I have done wrong to myself. Now I submit with Solomon to God, the Provider of the worlds.”

335

This is an important point. Our behavior is affected by the appreciation and admiration that our spirit has for another spirit that surpasses it in some respect. This admiration can decide the course that a person takes, and can determine their direction in life. That is because the appreciating and admiring spirit is indeed strictly attached to the spirit it admires, and always accompanies it heartily.

That is one of the firm rules of the spirit that was set down by its Creator. You shall find no replacement for God’s Rules, and you shall find no change in God’s Laws. However, this appreciation and reverence for others differs from one spirit to another, according to what one likes and what their spirit inclines to. Some spirits glorify others because of their science and knowledge, their possessions and authority, their perfection and noble morals, or for other considerations. That is because each person has preferred inclinations and favorite interests, on which they focus above anything else. For this reason, people only appreciate those who surpass them in these things, and who excel to a greater extent than them in these respects.

Indeed, the brothers of our master Joseph (pth)

-

and his parents too

-

appreciated his perfection because their spirits were fond of virtue and perfection, preferring them to anything else in this life.

As for Pharaoh’s magicians, who were experts in the science of magic: they revered the knowledge of our master Moses (pth) after he showed them what had frustrated their magic as a whole. No sooner had he thrown down his staff for it to swallow up their false devices than they prostrated themselves before him (pth).

Balqees, the queen of Sheba, prostrated herself to our master Solomon (pth). She only admired him because she had great possessions; the moment that she eyed his possessions, she admired and revered him because he surpassed her in this respect. Then her spirit bound up to his, submitting to Al’lah, the Almighty.

This admiration and spiritual submission causes what is folded in the superior spirits to be reflected onto the lesser spirits that appreciate them, and this quality is then imprinted on the pages of the latter spirits. The primacy of our master Joseph (pth) in loving Al’lah and knowing about His Attributes was reflected onto the spirits of his father, mother, and brothers, so that he became a leader for them in this field. The faith and knowledge that were folded in the spirit of our master Moses (pth) were reflected onto the spirits of the magicians, who then said what words they said, as we have mentioned previously. What happened between the queen of Sheba and our master Solomon (pth) was similar.

Thus, if you admire a person, you will surely enter through the same entrances that they enter, and will drink from the same springs from which they drink, so that their spiritual state will be impressed upon your own spirit. If they are a disbeliever or an infidel, the contents of their spirit will clearly manifest themselves in your own. However, if they possess perfection and faith, you will sense this perfection and enter with them through the entrances of true belief. That is why the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, invoking God:

“Oh, God of all! May You not let a disbeliever oblige me, lest my heart will love him.”

336

He (cpth) supplicated in this way because he knew the rules of the spirit, and so he was afraid that goodness might reach him at the hands of a disbeliever. If this happened, his heart (cpth) would incline to this disbeliever and then be affected by this disbeliever’s spiritual state.

Look at God’s Envoy (cpth), the master of creation, and how he fears and invokes this invocation so as to preserve the pureness of his spirit. What kind of state, then, would we find ourselves in, if our spirits were to appreciate and glorify people of infidelity, bawdiness and disbelief?! In contrast, how would our states be if our hearts were to incline to God’s Envoy (cpth), admiring and revering him?

These facts are also proved by the following saying of his (cpth):

“Man adopts his close friend’s faith; you should therefore be careful when choosing an intimate friend.”

337

However, the path of glorifying God’s Envoy (cpth) and appreciating the people of perfection who came after him as guides is not available to you unless you yourself are one of the people of perfection, for only the possessors of favor can appreciate it. Thus, if you want to accompany God’s Envoy (cpth) spiritually, you should think of these universal signs until you believe with certainty that there is no god but Al’lah.

If you really believe, your faith will prevent you from disobeying Al’lah, and will allow you to straighten yourself for His Orders. Then you will be confident that Al’lah is pleased with you, and your spirit will approach Him, the Almighty, and will derive perfection from Al’lah through communicating with Him. This will cause you to appreciate and praise those who surpass you in perfection, and you can then enter into the spirit of the master of the perfect ones (cpth) by means of them.

Appreciating God’s Envoy (cpth) and coupling with him enables your spirit to enter into God’s Presence through him, and to rise in the abodes of the Godly Love.

“Oh, serene spirit

(that is content with this lower life)

! Return to your Provider’s Guidance, pleased and pleasing to Him. Enter into the true spirits of My obedient followers

(ibad)

and enter My Paradise.”

338

Thus, the noble angels prostrated themselves before our master Adam (pth) when ordered to do so by Al’lah, the Almighty, and also because of the perfection that was folded in their spirits. No sooner had they realized Adam’s superiority and excellence in perfection and scientific knowledge than they all prostrated themselves before him.

As for the devil, he knew nothing of the Godly Perfection and acquired no scientific knowledge of Al’lah’s Attributes. The devil did not enter into God’s Presence once; nor did his spirit become colored with anything of the stain of perfection.

This foolish and ignorant one did not glorify his Provider. Therefore, when the Almighty ordered him to prostrate himself before our master Adam (pth), he:

“…rejected and disdained this. He was one of the disbelievers.”

339

The Holy Qur’an refers to the devil’s refusal and his arrogance in other verses, such as the following words of the Almighty:

“Then We said to the angels: prostrate yourselves before Adam. They prostrated themselves, except the devil who said: do I prostrate myself to one whom You have created out of mud?”

340

“We said to the angels: prostrate yourselves before Adam. Then they prostrated themselves, except the devil who was one of the jinn-kind; he disobeyed his Provider’s Command…”

341

Through these noble verses you can see that the devil’s refusal and his disdain for prostrating himself resulted from his disbelief in his Creator. Therefore he was blind to the truth, and the perfection of our master Adam (pth) was obscured from him.

You can also see that the devil was not a leader of the angels, as a group of oblivious people pretend, but was of the jinn-kind; nor had he any knowledge of His Creator’s Majesty, and therefore disobeyed his Provider’s Command.

Indeed, disbelief and a lack of perfection prevent the sight of the spirit from witnessing reality, confine it to perceiving only the form, and attach it to fancies. This is what happened to the the devil, who alleged that fire was better than mud, and did not know that knowledge of Al’lah is what raises one’s rank and exalts one above other creatures. The Almighty has indicated the unbelievers’ inability to witness reality and to recognize God’s Envoys (ptt) in His Saying in the following noble verse:

“…you find them looking at you, but they do not see you

(your reality)

.”

342

This was also indicated in what the people of Midian said to their Envoy, our master Sho’aib (pth):

“They said: you are surely bewitched. You are but a mortal like ourselves. Indeed, we believe that you are lying.”

343

This is what was said by the people of ‘Ad and Thamoud, and this is also what is said by each unbeliever, and this is the state of anyone who is far from Al’lah. From here on, it is clear to us that recognition of God’s Envoys (ptt) and their glorification

-

as well as that of the true guides

-

can only be achieved by a person after reaching true belief in God. This is a belief that is based on total realization. If a person glorifies and praises Al’lah the Almighty, and appreciates His Favor and Charity, they will approach Him and derive perfection from Him. Such a person will then admire those who possess perfection. He, the Great and the Almighty, is the First and the Last; He guides the heart of all who believe in Him, and lets them walk on the right path.

Al’lah the Almighty ordered our master Adam (pth) and his wife to dwell in Paradise, as indicated in the noble verse; God says:

“Then We said: oh, Adam! Dwell in Paradise-you and your wife-and eat whatever you want from it happily and freely. Never come near this tree in order not to be one of the unjust.”

344

The spirits of our master Adam and his wife (ptt) surrounded their two noble bodies so that their enjoyment of this lower life was spiritual, and the fruit would not have entered into their bellies as this would have required digestion and making an effort.

The word ‘Paradise’ does not refer to a place high up in the heavens where our master Adam (pth) first dwelled, but which he then had to leave, although this idea may come into people’s minds. The course of the verses disproves the idea that Al’lah caused him to descend to the earth on which we now live, for this conception does not agree with reality at all.

At the beginning of this account, the Almighty God mentioned that He had informed the angels of His Will, which was that he would make a successor to Him on earth when He said:

“…I am creating man from mud.”

345

Mud exists on earth, not in the heavens. Besides, the verses reported by Al’lah in the Holy Qur’an through which He reveals the origin of humanity and the beginning of creation also deny such a belief. Instead, they show that humans have been on the earth on which we now live since they were first created. God says:

“For God, the example of Jesus is like that of Adam; He created him from soil, then said to him ‘Be’ and he existed.”

346

“Al’lah has brought you forth from the earth like a plant and to the earth He will restore you; then He will bring you out of it afresh.”

347

“…it was He Who made you from the earth and gave you dwellings upon it…”

348

“From earth We have created you, and into earth We shall return you, and out of it We shall bring you once again.”

349

The Almighty created our master Adam and his wife from the earth and let them dwell in a Paradise upon it. Paradise is the hidden spiritual bliss which a person finds within themselves and enjoys, without it being revealed to any other people.

Then, our master Adam (pth) and his wife entered into God’s Presence, and were directed towards Him, and experienced a witnessing of the Godly Perfection that was incomparable to any other pleasure or bliss. That is what we can understand from the word ‘Paradise’, for the believing human spirit can find no pleasure, bliss, or tranquility like the pleasure, bliss, and tranquility that is experienced when looking at the Beauty of its Creator and witnessing His Loftiest Perfection.

Our master Adam (pth) and his wife sank into spiritual bliss and dwelled therein, and they were then in a state that is different from the material state in which we now live.

A person has a spirit, a soul and a body. The spirit in this worldly life is surrounded by and restrained within its body. It sees with the eyes, hears with the ears and tastes with the tongue. Since our bodily state has control over our spiritual one, a person can never live unless the body has its share of food, drink, and clothing. The body must inevitably make an effort to get what is needed, including comfort and sleep.

When Al’lah the Almighty brought our master Adam (pth) and his wife into being, they were in a state that was different to what people now experience. His spirit surrounded its body like the flame of a candle surrounds all sides of the wick. Because of this situation, he did not need ears to hear or eyes to see, nor did he need a tongue with which to taste, because all of his spirit was tasting, hearing and viewing. Besides that, his body was not in need of anything at that time, because there was no hunger or thirst, no heat or coldness, and neither toil nor fatigue. The spirit was put on the body and surrounded it, with its state overruling that of the body. Its entry into Al’lah’s Presence was perpetual, constant and unceasing.

By my life! That is the state of the dwellers in Paradise in the hereafter. Referring to the state of our master Adam at the beginning of his life, Al’lah says:

“Then We said: oh, Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you to leave Paradise lest you become tired; you neither feel hungry nor naked therein, and you do not feel thirsty, nor does the heat of the sun injure you.”

350

With regard to eating, our master Adam (pth) did eat while in this spiritual state

-

that is to say, in Paradise

-

but it was an eating made up of tasting, which is also how people will eat in Paradise in the afterlife. The rays of the spirit that surround the body flow to the fruit, constantly and continuously tasting it, just as the rays of the sun flow to the depths of water, with no need for the body of the sun to approach the lake or river in question.

This continuous tasting and eating may take a long time, sometimes lasting for months, but a person will never feel satiated or satisfied. The more the spirit is near to its Creator, the more its tasting and enjoyment of the things it eats will be, because its tasting and enjoyment will be proportional to its soundness and happiness.

This is the state of those who dwell in Paradise, which is the same state as that of our master Adam (pth) and his wife at the time they were brought into existence by Al’lah. They were in the Paradise of bliss, witnessing the great Godly Beauty. Besides this, their spirits were eating happily and freely from the earth; that is, they were constantly tasting, finding neither heaviness nor discomfort. The Almighty intervened to prevent our master Adam (pth) and his wife from approaching the tree; that is, He instructed them not to put the material of the fruit into their mouths. When material enters the mouth and then moves to the belly, it requires chewing and digestion, and consequently, a person’s state will change to another one, wherein the rule is with the body and the spirit retreats within. The spirit will then become encircled and surrounded, which requires effort, labor, and seeking out the needs and material necessities of the body. That is what is meant by the noble verse; God says:

“…never come near this tree in order not to be of the unjust”

351

: meaning unjust to yourselves, when you shall be tired from laboring.

This means: do not put this fruit near to your mouths, but instead, taste it and eat from it spiritually. If you put the fruit into your mouths, you shall oppress yourselves, exposing yourself to tiredness, toil, and effort to achieve the requirements of the body.

Yes, the spirits of our master Adam (pth) and his wife were put over their noble bodies, so that their enjoyment of this world was a spiritual taste. The fruits were not to enter into their bellies, for that entry requires digestion and hard work.

The Almighty warned them against the devil and his enmity, to which the noble verse refers when God says:

“Then We said: oh, Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you out of Paradise lest you would be tired.”

352

As mentioned before, our master Adam (pth) and his wife dwelt in the bliss of entering into Al’lah’s Presence and enjoying the witnessing of that Great Godly Beauty. They clung to it, seeking no alteration from that state. Can the enjoyment of viewing the Face of God be equal to any other bliss?! Shall a believer be satisfied with anything short of this?!

Here and from this point on, the devil was pleased to find an entrance through which he could enter in order to divert that noble Prophet from his Creator and cause him to descend from the state in which he existed. God says:

“The devil whispered to him saying: oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and to an immortal property?!”

353

: that is: may I guide you to the tree which, if you eat from it, will allow you to perpetuate this bliss and possess this state? Your spirit will not cease from entering into Al’lah’s Presence, and will attain everlasting direction to Him.

Then, he swore by the Almighty God that he was advising them both. However, since nobody appreciates the great except for the great, our master Adam (pth) was overcome by his love for God, and this caused him to forget His Advice. Al’lah says:

“We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his”

354

: that is: he only forgot Our Advice, and We found no intention or resolution of his to infringe Our Command by disobeying.

The situation with his wife was similar, and they both ate from the tree; that is, they ate its fruit by putting them in their mouths out of their love for Al’lah, so that their spirits shifted from one state to another. Their spirits followed the material that was entering their bodies, and became surrounded by the body having itself previously surrounded the body. Consequently they were in the state we are now experiencing (the worldly state), feeling the pain of hunger and suffering from thirst. God says:

“…when they tasted the tree

(fruit)

, their shameful deeds

(that displeased them)

appeared to them. They started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves. Their Provider called out to them, saying: did I not forbid you to approach that tree, and did I not warn you that Satan was a sworn enemy for you? They replied: oh our Provider, we have wronged ourselves, pardon us and have mercy on us, or we shall surely be among the lost.”

355

Returning to the verses of Al-Baqara Fortress, the following noble verse refers to the bodily state of our master Adam (pth) and his wife after they physically ate the fruit. Due to drawing far from God, the devil became envious and mean, and was incited to turn them away by his jealousy.

God says:

“Then, the devil made them lapse away from it and got them out of where they had been…”

The devil told Adam that his Provider had never advised him against the tree, telling him that if he ate, he would perpetually remain in his enjoyment of Paradise. Since our master Adam had no power of thought, he forgot God’s Command and ate, so that his spirit went inside and his approach towards Al’lah became obstructed.

The statement

“Then, the devil made them lapse away from it…”

is intended to show that he made them descend and shift from the state of spiritual tasting to the bodily state. In this way he drove them out of their previous state of eating made up of tasting, and their immaterial bliss. They then needed to fulfill bodily needs and material demands, about which they had never cared beforehand. Al’lah says:

“…We said: go hence, and may you be enemies to each other. The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while.”

356

As for the words

“…We said: go hence…”

this means that they had to go from the spiritual state: that is, descend to this lower life, where there is seeking after one’s livelihood and the making of effort to ensure that you meet the needs and demands that this life entails.

That was the new state in which our master Adam (pth) and his wife found themselves, and so it was with their children after them. This state

-

as is known to us

-

was completely different from the state in which they had been beforehand.

The statement:

“…and may you be enemies to each other…”

means that the unbeliever shall antagonize the believer, and demonstrates that the wisdom hidden behind this story is that it shows the enmity that the devil and his offspring

-

who have turned away from God

-

bear for humanity. Those of humankind who follow God’s Words shall see afterwards what the devil did to deceive our master Adam (pth), falsely swearing to him in order to try to turn him away from Al’lah. This will help these believers not to be deceived or tempted by the devil. Meanwhile, the unbelievers among Lucifer’s offspring

-

who are some of the jinn-kind

-

will be with him as enemies of Adam’s children, in order to turn them away from what is right so as to unsettle their faith.

The statement

“…and may you be enemies to each other…”

means that the devil will be an enemy of humanity. This statement aims to acquaint us with the fact that God, the Almighty, engineered humanity’s exodus to this worldly life in this way in order to give humans who are prepared for perfection a practical lesson about the devil’s enmity and deception. With this, they become acquainted with him and will be cautious about his temptation. All of that shows us the Compassion and the Clemency of God, the Almighty, for Al’lah is Clement and Merciful.

The statement

“…The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while”:

this refers to the human lifetime, and denotes that a person has a limited age and a certain moment of death. If their lifetime passes and their death comes, they will certainly leave this worldly life. On the contrary, a person’s life in the life to come is unlimited and lasts forever. That is because a person’s life in this world depends on the healthiness of their body and its maintenance, so that it is able to work. If the main systems stop working, the spirit will exit, following the soul. They will leave the body together, but the spirit will remain connected to it and will continue to observe it.

In the other abode, the spirit will have control since it will surround the body, and so the body will have no efficiency or function from that day forth, and will not be subject to senility or weakness or debility. It will only be something on which the spirit will rest on the day when it becomes the possessor of life. Since the spirit is a luminous essence that is not affected by what happens to the components of the body, such as weakness and dissolution, life in the other abode will be eternal, and will have neither limit nor end.

The statement

“…The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while”,

also serves to show that the existence of humanity on the earth has a certain term. When this term finishes, this life will finish with it, and then people will go to the other abode where each person will see the consequences of their deeds and their effort.

How Did Our Master Adam (pth) Forget the Advice of Al’lah, the Almighty, and How Could the Devil Have Deceived Him?

Can the devil enter into the spirits of Prophets? Do they disobey Al’lah? How can we find congruity between what our master Adam (pth) did when he ate from the tree, and what the Holy Qur’an proclaims about the impeccability of Prophets and the impossibility that a Prophet could contravene any of God’s Commands?

I say: these are serious points that have the potential to cause a lot of people to lose their footing. If a person does not fully understand this issue, and does not realize the perfection of God’s Envoys, their spiritual sublimity, and the impossibility that any Prophet could ever violate any of God’s Commands, this person will certainly slip and fall into the hell of shunning Al’lah. As long as such a person’s spirit is veiled off from witnessing the perfection with which the spirits of God’s Envoys (cptt) are colored, none shall be able to deliver them from their distance from Al’lah.

This is because the human spirit is naturally disposed, as we know, to love perfection. It cannot appreciate somebody or attach itself to somebody in a link of cordiality if it finds that there is a defect or deviation from the truth in this other person. That is one of the firm rules of the spirit.

To enter into the fields of certain spiritual belief and seeing by Al’lah’s Light, it is necessary to like God’s Envoys and accompany them heartily. Therefore, in entering into God’s Presence through being in such company, how would it be possible for a spirit to like and accompany these Envoys of God if it found even a single defect in them? How could such a spirit enter into God’s Presence by means of them? This spirit would undoubtedly remain far from Al’lah, veiled off from Him, and deprived completely of the opportunity to approach Him.

Therefore, to clarify these important points, we say:

In order to understand the first point, about how our master Adam (pth) forgot the Advice that was given to him by Al’lah, we should return to our master Adam’s original state. This refers to the first state of Adam in Paradise; the state of approaching God before moving to the lower worldly life; that is, before he descended from his high spiritual state to the bodily one which we are currently experiencing. We say:

Humans have thought and a mind in this world, whereas in Paradise, they are free of thought and only have a mind. Thought

-

that jewel with which Al’lah the Almighty has adorned humanity in this world, situating it in the brain

-

is now the means by which we attain knowledge and understand reality. The eye sees, the ear hears, and the tongue tastes, and then these sensations are transferred to the spirit, which sends the rays of these perceptions up into the brain, when it is true in seeking truth. There in the brain, the power of thought performs the processes of comparing, contrasting, disuniting and assembling; it is then that the spirit attains what it is demanding.

It is the power of thought that decides on the Existence of the Organizer through observing the cosmic discipline, deduces the Existence of the Actor through viewing the actions that it views, and reaches knowledge of the Provider because of His Provision. The spirit fully realizes these facts that are decided by the power of thought. The spirit witnesses them within itself and becomes certain of them, so that these facts are engraved on the page of the spirit and never leave it. It fully realizes the fact of the Godly Existence and then witnesses the Attributes of Al’lah, the Almighty. This is the utmost aim behind the existence of humanity in this lower worldly life. Thinking, therefore, is the processes of contrasting, comparing, disuniting and assembling that are performed by the brain so that it can discern realities and decide upon their existence.

Total Realization

Total realization here refers to the witnessing of these facts and viewing them with the eye of the spirit. When thinking is true and honest, it will surely lead its owner to total and full realization and the full entry of these facts into the mind at a fundamental level. These facts then remain stored in the memory and the spirit, so that when a person needs access to one of these truths, the rays of thought are reflected onto what the spirit has previously incorporated into its mind. The facts that were stored in the spirit shine upon it, and with that, the person recognizes and remembers them.

Speaking of thinking and the mind, we should give a brief statement through which we reveal the activity of thought and its ability to apprehend the facts. We say:

In order to achieve this realization of a particular matter, it is necessary for the spirit to concentrate on it, for the power of thought acts superficially in relation to matters in which the spirit is not entirely interested. This is also the case if the spirit is not completely true and insistent in its search. Without this total concentration, the power of thought cannot reach the point where it discerns reality, nor can it make a decision; consequently, the spirit remains far from total realization or witnessing. In order to let the spirit come to a stage of total realization in the case of knowing the Creator and Provider, and to believe without doubt that there is no god but Al’lah, and for the spirit to know that all the steering is in Al’lah’s Hand alone, it is necessary to acquaint the spirit with the fact that this lower life

-

with which it is pleased and content

-

ends quickly and terminates before long, and whatever a person collects in this life, and whatever they experience, they will surely die and leave the lower plane of existence. This is an actual fact which will certainly come to fruition.

If a person takes their example from their parents, relatives and forefathers who have come before them, and acquaints their own spirit with those who previously dwelled in their dwellings or used their place of business, but who have now passed on from this worldly life, this person’s spirit is being informed about death and its awesome effect, and about the grave and its loneliness, and such a lesson is being repeated on a daily basis. Such a spirit will be afraid and will stop indulging in love of this world and will desist from turning to the lower life. It will then seriously seek to know its Provider Who looks after it. The efforts of the spirit will gather with those of thought, acting hurriedly and searching earnestly. It will continually compare and contrast, disunite and reassemble, ask itself about itself and give answers until it reaches a decision about the existence of the Great Creator who has created everything. This person will continue researching until they come to believe that He, the Almighty, is the Supporter and Provider who provides for all creatures and supplies them with what they need in the twinkling of an eye, without forgetting any of them. Such a person will fully realize these facts in their spirit, and it will be a realization based on witnessing, and will be beyond all doubt.

Finally, this true thought moves from knowing the Provider to knowing the Steering God Who directs all the universe, deciding that the steering of the whole universe is in the Hands of Al’lah, and that there is no god but Al’lah. The spirit then realizes these facts and truly becomes a believing spirit. Indeed, belief is one of the results of realization, and one who realizes nothing has neither belief nor faith.

Thus, realization has the most important status in reaching true belief; it is achieved only after profound thinking. Thinking is not accomplished until a person is honest in seeking knowledge (or seeking knowledge of Al’lah), and nor do its wheels rotate until this point is reached. This truth is only attained by fearing death and its consequences.

As we have mentioned before, that is why Mohammad (cpth) lay on his right side and turned his face toward Al-Ka’ba while he was in the mosque, between the prayer of Sunna and the one which takes place at dawn. He was imitating our position in the tomb, thinking and teaching how to be true and then to reach belief. He (cpth) said:

“Mention that which ends the pleasures

(death)

frequently.”

357

He also admonishes people through his noble saying:

“Live as much as you like, for you shall certainly die; love whoever you like, for you shall truly leave them; do whatever you like, for you shall indeed be recompensed for it.”

358

This is so that a person may be guided and follow the way of belief, and death should be all the lesson and reminder we need.

This is a brief statement which must be mentioned insistently to anyone who wants to learn a lesson (or to be encouraged) and to reach true belief, and subsequently to understand the Qur’an, the Speech of the Great Provider.

Returning to the research we began while talking about our master Adam (pth), his eating from the tree, and how he forgot Al’lah’s Advice, we say:

In our earlier research we clarified that in this world, people have a mind and the power of thought, but in Paradise, they are free from thought and only have a mind. That is because the activity of thought depends on the functioning of the brain and the running of blood through it. You could also say that thought aids the spirit and helps it to achieve perception of the facts and realization of them. This is the case for as long as such a spirit is confined within its body in this world, and as long as this body has control and authority over it. However, if the spirit escapes from the body and wears the body, so that it surrounds it and becomes its ruler, then all of the bodily systems

-

including thought

-

will stop functioning. In this case, these apparatuses and this power of thought would have no function, and the spirit would realize reality by itself, without the need for thought or sensation.

In this lower life, a person remembers the incidents that happened to them and the deeds that they did by means of thought. Thought sends its rays to the spirit in order to shed light on these facts, and then the spirit remembers them. However, in the life to come, thought will stop functioning, so this person will not remember through thinking; instead, what they see will go into their mind. Therefore, when the deeds a person has performed in this life are shown to them, the spirit will fully realize them; that is to say, it will realize what was imprinted on itself by its own actions. That was the state of our master Adam (pth). His spirit surrounded his body and realized what it saw. Then the devil came to him and said:

“…Oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity

(to continually see the face of God)

, and to an immortal sublime property?”

359

: that is, may I guide you to a tree, and if you eat from this tree, your spirit will abide in the lofty state of constant entrance into Al’lah’s Beauty, and you shall have access to that beautiful and exalted state perpetually?

Then, when he swore by God to our master Adam (pth) that he was giving him advice, Adam (pth) forgot that God had forbidden him to eat from the tree, just as he forgot that the Almighty had cautioned him against the devil.

Our master Adam (pth) forgot all of this, which is normal, since on that day he had no power of thought with which to remember.

God says:

“We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his.”

360

that is, God did not find any intention to disobey in Adam.

The forgetting of our master Adam (pth) and his wife were imposed by the spiritual state in which they were, and in this case it was not a breach. Anyone who was in the same spiritual state as our master Adam (pth) at that time would do as he (pth) did. This was before he went into the physical state in which we now exist. His status inevitably decreed his actions and reactions, and this cannot be regarded as an infringement of God’s Orders or a breach of His Advice.

The Almighty God let our master Adam (pth) pass through this event, and made him and his wife two pivots of this story. His only purpose was to ensure that their offspring would be acquainted with the devil’s enmity and tricks when they were in the physical state, and furthermore, to give them a practical lesson by giving them a real example of this. In this way, their children were warned against the devil and his enmity. The noble verse refers to this; God says:

“Children of Adam! Let Satan not deceive you, as he got your parents out of Paradise…”

361

You may ask: if the matter was as you have explained, then what is the correct interpretation of the noble verse which mentions this occurrence, when God says:

“…and Adam disobeyed his Provider; then he has gone astray.”

?

362

We say: we have already revealed that our master Adam’s spiritual state had its own particularities and specificities which do not apply to the physical state in which we now exist. Adam had not reached this physical state at that time. When he forgot the advice, this was an outcome of his spiritual state at that time due to the absence of thought. Thus our master Adam’s eating from the tree can never be regarded as an infringement within the meaning that we now understand by the term, in our worldly state, no matter what strikes the minds of those who did not know the rank of God’s Envoy (pth).

To understand this verse, we have to understand the noble verses that come before and after it, which are mentioned in the course of this story when God says:

“We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his. When We said to the angels ‘prostrate yourselves before Adam’, they prostrated themselves, except for Lucifer who rejected this. Then We said: oh Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you to leave Paradise lest you become tired; you neither feel hungry nor naked therein, and you do not feel thirsty, nor does heat of the sun injure you. The devil whispered to him saying: oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity

(to continually see the face of God)

, and to an immortal property?! They both ate from it, so their shameful deeds

(that displeased them)

appeared to them and they started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves. And Adam disobeyed his Provider; then he has gone astray. His Provider then chose him, forgave him, and gave him guidance.”

363

These noble verses clarified to us that our master Adam (pth) only forgot the Advice of God and did not intend to disobey. He (pth) ate from the tree desiring only to perpetuate his existence in Paradise, which is (as previously mentioned) the bliss of entering into God’s Presence and enjoying the witnessing of His Beauty. The only motive that drove him to eat from the tree was his love for Al’lah and his wish to continue to abide in the bliss of entering into His Presence.

As for the statement

“Adam disobeyed his Provider; then he has gone astray”,

its meaning becomes plainly understood if we join it to the statement

“They both ate from it, so their shameful deeds

(that displeased them)

appeared to them and they started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves…”:

that is, as soon as our master Adam (pth) and his wife ate from the tree, their physical states appeared to them, and due to the emergence of such a state, our master Adam (pth) remembered Al’lah’s Advice. This remembrance occurred because this bodily state is associated with the existence of thought, which in turn causes remembrance to occur. At that time, he (pth) knew that the state in which he found himself resulted only from his infringement of the Advice of God and his forgetting of His Order.

The Purpose of the Tale of Our Master Adam (pth)

It is:

To teach love of God.

To teach us not to listen to the devil.

The statement

“…and Adam disobeyed his Provider…”

means that no sooner had the bodily state come over our master Adam (pth) than he realized in his spirit that he had forgotten what Al’lah, the Almighty, had advised him, and that he had acted contrary to that Advice.

The statement

“…and Adam disobeyed his Provider…”

is not a substantiation of Adam’s disobedience, nor is it a confirmation of infringement. Instead, it describes the state of our master Adam, and reveals his sense and his spiritual perception of falling into disobedience, because of forgetting the Godly Advice.

As to the words

“…then he has gone astray”,

the word ‘astray’ is derived from ‘straying’, which is to be converted or to turn away from a high state, including happiness and goodness, to a lower one, causing discomfort and wretchedness. God says:

“But the generations who succeeded them neglected communication with Al’lah and succumbed to temptation; these shall assuredly go astray”

364

: that is: they shall find degradation relative to the position of their forefathers because they neglected to communicate with Al’lah and followed their own desires, and so they shall face troubles and wretchedness.

Mohammad (cpth) often introduced his sermons with his noble saying:

“He who obeys Al’lah and His Envoy is on the right path, but he who disobeys Al’lah and His Envoy goes astray, until he returns to God’s Order.”

365

Accordingly we say that when our master Adam (pth) saw the bodily state in which he ended up, and when he remembered that he had infringed his Provider’s Advice, his spirit became ashamed of this infringement and was veiled off from the state of entering into God’s Presence because of the shyness which occupied his spirit at this time.

We can understand from the statement:

“…Adam disobeyed his Provider; then he has gone astray”

that Adam (pth) had realized, in his spirit, that he had disregarded his Provider’s Advice, and with that, his spirit was ashamed and veiled off from entering into God’s Presence, and so Adam turned away from the high state in which he had been. At that moment, his Provider called him, revealing to him that his eating from the tree was dependant on a high intention. This intention was Adam’s desire for his state

-

whereby he was constantly in the presence of God’s Beauty

-

to continue in perpetuity, and the wish to continue being with Al’lah. Such high intention and elevated purpose is not considered to be disobedience, nor does it entail shame or diffidence, especially when associated with that original spiritual state which necessitates forgetting due to the absence of thought. Through acquainting our master Adam (pth) with these facts, the Almighty willed Adam’s return to Him and the driving away of the shyness which had occupied his spirit. That is what we can understand from these words:

“Then his Provider chose him…”

366

: that is, He made him return to Him with his heart wholly engaged with Him, the Almighty.

That is also what the noble verse reported in the Cow Fortress indicates wherein the Almighty says:

“Then Adam received words from His Provider…”

that is, words that revealed to him his noble intention and elevated purpose. This was to dispel shyness from his spirit. With that, he knew that Al’lah, the Almighty, did not blame him for his forgetting and did not consider his action on an external basis, instead looking inside at the reality and the intention that was folded within this action, for verily, deeds are evaluated according to intentions.

Our master Adam (pth) submitted to God, and then the Almighty inspired his spirit so:

“Oh, Adam! Your intention is noble and high. We never blame you for what came out of you.”

Similarly, whoever falls into infringement unintentionally can easily return to God, but those who do so insistently and with intention have no way to return.

Adam, then, realized that he had not disobeyed his Provider, nor had he determined to infringe His Rules, and he realized that Al’lah is Omniscient and knows all of our intentions. With that, his spirit became tranquil and was sure of God’s satisfaction with it once again. He returned to his Provider, entering into His Presence and directing himself wholly to Him. His Provider then accepted his repentance and raised the veil of shyness off his spirit, restoring him to his original state of witnessing the Godly Beauty and Perfection. This is indicated in the noble verse when God says:

“…and He made him repent

(He accepted his repentance)

…”

that is Al’lah’s Care, surrounding our master Adam (pth) and maintaining him, and manifesting itself clearly in this tale. That is how the Almighty treats all His creation (ibad). He sends them what will make their straying spirits return to Him to enjoy the everlasting bliss He has prepared for them. That is what we understand by the statement

“…He is the Repenter, the Merciful”

367

: meaning that He displays the kind of treatment that will allow us to return to Him.

Observe, then, God’s Sympathy and Compassion, and think about His great Grace for His creation (ibad). He decided to make our master Adam (pth) His successor on earth before He brought him into this world, and before He brought his offspring out from his back when he was in a spiritual state. Then He made his transition from that spiritual state to this bodily one take place in a way in which He showed the honour of this Envoy (pth) and his great love for his Creator; besides which, with the tale of this first man, the Almighty gave lasting examples and lessons to his children by making him stand before his offspring as the first tutor. He fulfilled His Will in such a way as to acquaint people with the rules of the spirit on which entry into God’s Presence is based. He let them know the way in which the spirit can return to the field of sacredness so that, if their spirits become shy and draw away in diffidence, they shall be able to return if they only revive their confidence and dispel shame from themselves.

As we have previously mentioned, the Almighty also wanted to acquaint us with the enmity of the devil, so we would be aware of his cunning and trickery.

Now can one who opposes, after all of that, object and disparage this noble Envoy (pth) or impute Al’lah with cruelty towards humanity? Truly He, the Almighty, always tries to return His creation (ibad) to the right way:

“…yet the unbelievers wrangle about Al’lah, though He tries a lot with them.”

368

This is just some of what we have understood from this story, and how many examples and lessons and their like have been included!

“Those examples We give to oblivious people, but none will get them into mind except the scientists of Al’lah’s Attributes.”

369

We have answered the questions we have previously mentioned, detailing and demonstrating that our master Adam (pth) did not disobey his Provider, and that his original spiritual state necessitated forgetting the Advice he had received. This proves to us that what our master Adam (pth) and his wife did when they ate from the tree was based, indeed, on a high intention, as the devil swore to them

-

by God

-

that they would stay forever in that state of pleasant witnessing and magnificent entry into God’s Presence if they did what he said and ate from the tree. Since this Prophet (pth) did not recognize that the devil was lying, he believed what the devil was saying and forgot Al’lah’s Advice to him.

“…Provider, may You not be angry with us if we forget or lapse into error…”

370

Our master Mohammad (cpth) said:

“Punishment was raised off my people for lapses into error, forgetting, and for what they were impelled to do.”

371

Al’lah says:

“God chose Adam, Noah, the Abrahams and the Imrans above all the worlds”:

these families were selected by the Almighty above all the worlds in order to guide people to Al’lah. What was this choice based on?

The Almighty set this forth in the Imran Fortress, saying:

“They are the offspring of one another…”:

they are all of one origin, they are Adam’s sons, but

“…Al’lah is All-Hearing, Omniscient”

372

: He did not choose them haphazardly, but can hear everything that they say, and the Omniscient knows everything about their intentions and states. He selected them because their states were elevated and their guidance was high. If your intention is high and your words are also, Al’lah will bestow His Favor upon you.

Thus, anyone who talks about the Prophets and who wrongs or mistrusts them indeed denies the statement

“…Al’lah is All-Hearing, Omniscient”,

or, in other words, such a person thinks that Al’lah, the Almighty, chose Adam in a haphazard way, knowing nothing about him. Of course this is untrue.

The Almighty God chose these people for their perfect lofty spirits, as a guide should be a perfect person. Anyone, then, who talks about the Prophets and offends them has no faith.
