If a person really believes that Al’lah hears all and knows all, they will not talk about Al’lah’s Envoys in an evil way, for Al’lah hears every creature and scientifically knows their state: He chose His Envoys (ptt) because of their pure spirits and high intentions.

Returning to the Hadith of God’s Envoy (cpth), who never speaks out of his own fancy, we find that his lofty saying tells us:

“Without pride, I am the master of Adam’s sons on the Day of Resurrection, and-without pride-the banner of praising Al’lah is in my hand. On that Day, there is no Prophet-Adam and all who are below him-who does not join me (and is under my banner), and-without pride-I am the first intercessor.”

373

Here we understand that Adam (pth) is in second position concerning loftiness, exaltedness and elevation of rank. He is above all other Envoys and Prophets but is below the master of creation, our master Mohammad (cpth). Just like all the devout Prophet masters below him, he is impeccable of error or the commission of either great or minor sins, and incapable of disobeying Al’lah or infringing His Command, for He, the Almighty, says of all the Prophets:

“…But they are purified and strictly true obedient followers (ibad). They do not speak before Him, and by His Order they act.”

374

He is the Prophet and the Envoy that was first created, and the Almighty addressed him in His Noble Saying about the angels:

“…tell them about their Attributes...”

375

He is a Prophet and an Envoy sent forth by Al’lah to the responsible jinn (who accepted bearing the Trust in Al-Azal world) and to the whole and noble angels, as well as to humanity, beginning with his noble offspring. The purpose behind this story is to warn people against the cunning of the devil, and that is merely out of the Almighty’s Sympathy, Compassion and Clemency.

§§§§§

We have to understand two points arising from the discussion of the questions mentioned above. If we perceive them correctly, all matters that are misunderstood by many people will be driven out of our minds.

The first one is about the meaning of the noble verse which is found in this story in the Almighty’s Words:

“So, he

(the devil)

let them down with deception…”

376

Could the devil have caused our master Adam (pth) and his wife to be deceived?! On the contrary, could this verse have a delicate meaning that is appropriate to the position and perfection of this noble Envoy?!

Replying to this, we say: the words

“So, he let them down…”

are taken from ‘to let down’; that is, you can say that someone let down the branch, meaning that they brought it near to themselves. Thus, when the devil swore to our master Adam (pth) that eating from the tree would make him attain perpetual residence in Al’lah’s Presence, in total possession of that state, he made him (pth) approach the tree and eat from it with his wife.

As for the words

“…with deception…”,

they do not refer to our master Adam; rather they refer to the devil himself, as it was the devil’s spirit that was engaged in deception, and not the spirit of our master Adam (pth).

In detail we say: deception is a spiritual state that prevails over a person’s spirit, making them suppose that a thing is true, whereas this is not the reality. For example, when a person is deceived by the moonlight at night, when they wake up and watch the moon rising they may suppose that the dawn is about to come although it is still midnight. A person may also be deceiving themselves if they think that they are powerful and knowledgeable, although in fact they have no knowledge except what Al’lah has taught them, and have no power except through Al’lah.

Thus, the devil was deceiving himself; he thought that by swearing by Al’lah and claiming that eating from the tree would make our master Adam’s residence with Al’lah something that lasted forever, he would be able to make our master Adam (pth) disobey his Provider, causing Adam to become shy and distant from Al’lah. However, the subsequent events were in conflict with his aim and supposition, for our master Adam’s elevated intention was a steady basis on which he depended, allowing him to return and resort to Al’lah. Meanwhile, the devil came out of this trial humiliated and expelled.

This made it clear to us that the devil was unable to deceive our master Adam (pth) or make him distant from Al’lah. The meaning of the words

“…with deception…”

describe the state of the devil when he imagined that he could be successful. However, events did not match his supposition, and he was turned away in failure and disappointment.

Concerning the second point, you might ask: how could the devil throw his whispers at our master Adam (pth) although our master Adam is unceasingly entering into Al’lah’s Presence?! Can we regard this accident as proof that Satan can enter into the Prophets?!

To reply to this question and illustrate this point we say: this matter becomes absolutely clear and obvious to us if we return to the original state of humanity, when Adam’s spirit was surrounding his body, and compare this spiritual state to the bodily one in which we now exist. When our master Adam (pth) was in the Paradise of entering into Al’lah’s Presence, his spirit was wearing his body and surrounding it. Because of this there was no screen to veil his spirit from the spirit of the devil. Instead, his spirit was visible and uncovered. However, since our master Adam was always entering into Al’lah’s Presence and constantly witnessing Him, the devil could do no more than throw his whispers at Adam, and talk to him from a distance without approaching him, as he did. For example, if I was walking in the street and heard a word whispered from a distance, or a word that someone wanted me to hear which they wanted to affect my spirit, surely this would not be regarded as this person entering into me; nor would their speech and whispering be considered as the domination of their spirit over my spirit. It would be mere words and speech, the waves of which issued out of one spirit and hit the sheet of a second spirit, although there was a considerable distance between the two spirits.

Similarly, wireless radio stations may broadcast their waves from an area in the far east and be reflected by other receiving sets in the far west, although there is a large distance between the two locations. Indeed, this example perfectly clarifies to us the point we are talking about, and reveals that the devil did not draw near to our master Adam (pth) or enter into his spirit. He could not approach him, because he (pth) was continuously tending towards Al’lah. The fact is that the devil only whispered to him from a distance.

According to this meaning, the verse is plain in God’s Saying:

“The devil whispered to him…”

377

God did not say:

“he whispered into his chest”

or

“in his spirit”,

as when He says:

“Who whispers in the chests of oblivious mankind”

378

that is, those who are disconnected from Al’lah, the Almighty.

It is clear that the preposition ‘to’ indicates separation while ‘in’ indicates a circumstance of inclusiveness. This whispering

-

delivered from a distance

-

can never be taken as the entry of the devil into our master Adam (pth), or his drawing near to Adam. This story can never be regarded as proof of the ability of the devil to enter into the Prophets.

Finally, we must illustrate how the devil can never approach the Prophets in their bodily state. They are like all the rest of humankind in terms of how their bodies surround and control their spirits. They are born just like anyone else, and their bodies are exposed to the same conditions that affect others, such as good health or disease, youth and old age, weakness, senility and death.

As for their spirits (ptt), they have a constant tendency to Al’lah, and they have become devoted to that Lofty Presence due to their knowledge of the Tenderness and the Mercy that Al’lah has for everything in His creation, and their witnessing of His Perfection and His unlimited Beauty. Such being the case, they are always overwhelmed with the Godly Revelation, and are constantly covered with that light, without cessation.

In this bodily state, since the spirit is surrounded by the body, the devil’s whisper can never reach it from afar. He has to penetrate the spirit through the body, passing through the chest. However, the bodies of the Prophets are always overwhelmed by the Godly Light that comes to their spirits, due to their extreme truthfulness before Al’lah and their great love for Him. Therefore, the devil can never approach them, nor can he penetrate this Godly Light. Through this Revelation they (ptt) are safe in an inaccessible fort and a forbidding shelter from the devil.

Thus, we have revealed that Satan has no way at all to enter into the Prophets. Besides this, he has no way to reach any believer as long as their spirit is entering into Al’lah’s Presence, tending towards Him or being joined with His honourable and loyal Prophets. Al’lah guides a person to this means by which one can be rid of the devil.

“When Satan inspires evil to you, seek refuge in God; He hears all and knows all. When those who see by Al’lah’s Light are touched with the evil of Satan, they remember

(Al’lah)

and then they become enlightened.”

379

He says:

“No power has he

(Satan)

over believers who put their trust in their Provider. He has power only over those who befriend him and those who obey other gods besides Him

(Al’lah)

.”

380

§§§§§

Now, having answered these delicate questions, we should address a new point which can be summarized by the following question. We say:

Was the coming of our master Adam (pth) to this lower life, followed by the rest of humanity, for the best? Would it have been better for him to stay in Paradise, and for the rest of humanity to have been created therein, without allowing them to enter into the lower life? Which of the two states would have brought about more happiness and goodness for humanity?

To reply to this question, we say that this point can be cleared up for us if we return to the words about Paradise and its reality, and take into consideration the fact that people’s grades in Paradise shall be proportional to their deeds. For more detail we give the following example. Suppose that a man was traveling by train, and the windows of the train overlooked the most beautiful scenery, so that he was looking upon amazing wonders and marvels created by Al’lah. He could see gardens and trees, rivers and seas, charming scenes and various beautiful cities, the like of which viewers have never seen or imagined before. As long as this train kept running, without stopping, you would see this traveling man craning his neck towards these sights, desiring never to turn away because of their constant novelty and dissimilarity. You would see that he would not stop looking out the window, being careful not to lose sight of any of these wonders. However, if this train stopped for a length of time, you would find that this traveler would turn away from the window, no matter how beautiful and pleasant the sight before him was.

This is because the spirit which God the Almighty has created and made of endless capacity begins to feel tired if it is kept in the same state, and the human spirit is disposed to curiosity. If a person remains in the same state, they will become bored, because a beautiful thing which does not change becomes wearisome and even loathsome; the repetition of the same delightful and melodious thing renders it undesirable and boring.

In line with what we have mentioned, we say: since a person’s ascension and upward movement in the bliss of their entrance into God’s Presence depend (as previously mentioned) on the good deeds they have rendered in their worldly life, this means that if the human had been created in Paradise without coming to this lower world, there would be no deeds by which we could approach our Creator; nor would we have been able to ascend from one state to a higher one, and from one Paradise to another that is wider and loftier than the one before. The human race would have remained at one degree, and would never have exceeded it.

The Almighty God created the human spirit and granted it the greatest and the most abundant of all donations. He gave it the ability to advance gradually in its witnessing of the Godly Perfection, and to enjoy it increasingly, with no limit or end. The Envoy (cpth) clarified this in a Holy Saying when God said:

“Not My earth or My heaven could know Me, but the heart of My believing obedient follower could.”

Then, He

-

the Almighty

-

brought this human spirit to this world and gave it a wide scope of action, in order for it to qualify for this endless witnessing and this rising through the levels. He created yearning to be a motive for action that gives it a certain value. For example, if somebody does not yearn for money, then charity will have no meaning or effect for the spirit. The same applies to the chastity of one’s gaze at the men or women God has forbidden us to look at.

With that, the Almighty God has made this human fit to attain the greatest share of Godly Favor and eternal bliss, which no other being can ever attain. Such being the case, was not our exodus to this world a favor and a grace of God?

Is not it better than keeping us in a single Paradise? Instead of one high Paradise with obtainable fruit, God has given us endless high Paradises, of increasing and ascending lofty pleasure, into which the spirit sinks eagerly due to their variety and their superiority above one another in their sublimity and dignity. The viewer tastes them in delight, with a heart filled with love for the great Merciful God Who continues to overwhelm them with a bliss loftier than the one that came before.

Thus, there will be no boredom and no tiredness; on the contrary, there will be pleasure mixed with cheerfulness, in addition to increasing height and nearness to the Benefactor and Merciful, moving from one Paradise to endless others. The ladders with which this believer will climb from one level to another are their own deeds, mixed together with humanist intentions.

In the noble verse, God reveals that bringing the human race into the lower world was better than if they had remained in the state in which our master Adam (pth) began. God says:

“Sons of Adam! We have sent down upon you clothing that covers your shameful deeds and feathers, and the garment of piety is better. That is one of God’s Revelations; perchance they will remember.”

381

The garment of piety which Adam (pth) had is better than his original state. Similarly, taking a child out of their comfortable home and sending them to school, where there are restrictions and pressures, is better for them than keeping this child at home, where they are free and unrestrained. That is because their elevation is accomplished by education. If they do not go to school, they will never achieve any elevation or ascent.

The worldly life is a school that leads to elevation, both in this life and in the life to come. Our master Adam (pth) started off enjoying only a single Paradise, but after his worldly life he gained access to many levels of Paradise, rising increasingly towards better and more perfect ones with a desirable and lovely continuity; that is to say, he has gained endless Paradises instead of a single Paradise.

CHAPTER SIX

Way of Belief and True Faith.

Conclusion.

Way of Belief and True Faith

This universe contains the sun and the moon, the planets and stars, rain and ice, clouds and winds, animals and plants, the heavens and even the earth in its circular orbit, the four seasons with their changes and successions, and night and day with their differences and alternation. That is to say, the universe contains this multitudinous world filled with all its creatures and beings. This includes your body, composed of its systems and organs, and the commutation, dissolution and composition that happen inside it. Its glands perform the necessary secretions and the body prepares the different substances it requires. The universe is filled with everything that you know and everything that you do not know, and runs according to firm rules and strict discipline.

Therefore, if the Great Creator has laid down a law for this universe with all its creatures, and a system to be followed and not to be broken, and if this Great Creator has taken that same universe and subjugated it for humans, is it then possible or believable that human beings, the noblest of all creatures, have no law or statute to follow? Has the Great Creator arranged the entire universe, only to leave humankind to live in this life without guidance or order? Has the Great Creator put this entire universe in order, and then neglected humanity and let them astray in the darkness, unable to distinguish between that which benefits them and that which hurts them, not knowing how to proceed through the unknown of this life? It is undoubtedly true that right thought, sound logic, and sane understanding decree and confess the existence of a law which has been planned for humankind. The question, then, is: where is that law and order?

Let us consider what all the noble Envoys brought from God. Let us listen to the first verses with which the Almighty Al’lah inspired the Envoy (cpth), so that he (cpth) could inform people. God says:

“Recite in the Name of your Provider who created man from clots! Recite! Your Provider is the Most Bountiful One, who taught by imprinting

(referring to the instincts and the yearnings which God created in the spirits of humanity)

, taught man what he does not know.”

382

Let us think deeply about these words which the Envoy (cpth) disseminated to all the Arabs and all the nations. Let us meditate on that sign to which the Envoy (cpth) led his noble companions, and let us study the Qur’anic verses sent from Al’lah which he (cpth) recited to the people in Mec’ca in the first days of his mission. Let us look as one who is thirsty for truth looks, rather than as one who is clinging to what their forefathers followed, without perception or thinking. Let us leave behind the ignorance which has been fabricated by some people through whims and misguidedness.

Let us return to righteousness, for it is only righteousness that should be followed. Let us be guided by the noble Envoys and adopt the straight path that they all adopted before us. When you do that, you will discover the required order and the law that is decided for humanity in the Qur’an. It was this same law which the Envoy (cpth) himself applied, and which he called all his noble companions to apply. In this way they achieved high rank, and became known all over the world. This was how they gained the happiness and boons they gained.

I say, to apply this law and order is to consider your origin and to think of your beginning, because those who recognize themselves will recognize their Provider. When they recognize their Provider, He will guide them to the way of happiness and protect them from misery and loss. Therefore, those whom God guides are the ones who have adopted the straight path, but those who go astray from God will find no other lord than Him.

Oh! Think of your origin, for thinking of your origin and your beginning is the first article of this law and order which Al’lah has legislated for you.

Think! Why do you not think, since your Provider has granted you such a precious jewel to help you in thinking, to lead you to know your Creator and Provider?

Think! Why do you not think, when He has given you the great signs and the amazing discipline of this universe, with wide fields and large scope, in which your thought can be absorbed and roam?

Think! Why do you not think, since the universe is an open book before you? You can read even if there is no teacher to teach you or no one to tend to you, because Almighty Al’lah is the best Teacher and Guide for you, as long as you are truthful.

Think of your origin when you were semen in your father’s back. Consider this semen: how was it formed? Of what is it composed? Consider this semen: where was it put, and where did it settle? Think of yourself when you were in that safe haven, the deep darkness of the womb. Think of those stages through which you have passed: from semen to a clot, from a clot to a lump of flesh, from a lump of flesh to bones. Consider how these bones have been arranged in good order and consistency. The muscles have been fixed upon the bones, and from them have been made holes for the brain, the eyes, the ears and the mouth, a cavity for the heart and one for the lungs, and vessels for the intestines, and centers for the veins and for the sinews.

Think! I do not want to develop this in great detail. I shall let you witness and see how semen, made from an extract of different fruits, has turned into a balanced human being and a noble creature.

Think of and appreciate the greatness of the Hand which created and formed you. It made these organs for you, creating the brain, the heart, the main systems of the body, their bone structure, and all of the different components, and placed them in a safe place and a protected fort.

Think of that Hand which nourished you when you were just coming into this world, alone and without any power or strength. You were unable to provide for yourself, and indeed, nobody could provide for you except the Hand which watched over your creation. It is that Hand which provided for you, delivering food to you and supplying each of your organs with its necessary subsistence.

Think of that Hand, which was able to turn you from semen into a perfect person within just a few months, so that Its creation would neither be delayed nor premature in forming a human being within the appointed term.

Then, when the time of birth and entry into this world approached, It turned you upside down in your mother’s belly, placing your head facedown and your legs upwards, thus paving the way for your birth.

God says:

“Man has been killed. What makes him disbelieve? From what thing has He created him? From semen He has created and estimated him, then He paved the way for him, then He let him die and entombed him, then, if he will, He brings him to life. Is not it so? He

(man)

has not yet applied what He

(Al’lah)

has ordained for him.”

383

Having come into this new world and this new land, think how He endowed you with your mother’s sympathy and kindness, and put love and tenderness for you in her heart. He prepared your food in her breasts and made it pleasant, luscious and nourishing to drink, containing all the subsistence needed and required by your body.

Think of those meals and aliments which that Merciful Hand made for you. It increased their nutritional proportions moment by moment and meal after meal, in a way that was appropriate to your growth and your advances in years. Then, when your body required more nourishment and your stomach became able to digest solid foods, He raised your milk teeth, one tooth after another, according to what was required by growth and necessity.

After this, when you were seven years old, in order to build a body that would be ready for serious situations and great deeds, and to create a mind that could manage heavy affairs, He replaced your milk teeth with standard ones to process the food that would be necessary for this human body.

Think of that Hand which is still providing for you up until now. It sends the hot sunrays into the sea in order to vaporize the water. It then moves the winds to drive the clouds and rouse them from their lurking places, gathering them and piling them up in masses through which drops of water pour down, expressing God’s cordiality towards His creatures.

Once the dead earth is revived and irrigated after its thirst, It drives away the clouds and reveals the clear sky and the shining sun.

This allows the plants to begin their growth, and it is then that the land grants lavish blessings. God says:

“Have you considered the fact that you cultivate? Is it you that give it growth, or We? If We pleased, We could turn it into chaff. Would you then keep amusing yourselves or would you say: ‘We have incurred a loss. Indeed, we have deprived ourselves’? Have you considered the water which you drink? Was it you that poured it from the clouds, or We? If We pleased, We could turn it saline; will you then give thanks?”

384

Consider the foods and their various kinds, and the flowers and their forms and smells, and the varieties of fruit and their colors and tastes. Consider the four seasons and their alternation. Consider sleep and how God the Almighty has made it a period of cessation of feeling. Consider the day and how He made it a means of subsistence. Think of the air which helps you to breathe and inhale, and which provides the oxygen needed for burning materials. Think of the sun which supplies you with heat and light. Think of the seas and rivers, plains and mountains, animals and plants, clothes and covering, wool, cotton and flax. Think of this Hand, which fulfills all your requirements and keeps rearing you, showering you with its blessing, overwhelming you with its favor, and supplying you with provision, one moment after another without any cessation.

Think in this way and think of this Providence, for it was through such thought and reflection that our master Abraham took his first step in the way of belief. Through such thinking, our master Adam (pth) and our master Mohammad (cpth) and all the noble Envoys who came through the ages started on their path to belief.

Think! If you did, you would be guided and would know that there is a Great Provider who looks after you and never neglects you even for the twinkle of an eye. This Provider continued to provide for you from the time that you were an embryo until you became an infant, and then a young child, and then a complete human being. Therefore His Sustenance to you is permanent, and His Charity keeps successively flowing over you. If these things settle inside your spirit so that they have fully entered into your mind and you have ascertained their reality, a new field and a different way of thinking will open before you.

If this were to happen, you would see that your body will not remain either strong or fortitudinous, and that you will not live forever. Thus it was for your relatives who have left this life and passed away. So is it with your neighbor, who has parted from spouse and children and met death, after enjoying the worldly life for only a few years. Furthermore, your friends were not able to take pleasure in their stores or in the houses which they built. Death killed all their hopes in this life, and so they died at their appointed times without delay. There are those who have died after sickness, others after trouble, and others suddenly and unexpectedly. You remember this one and that one, the kings and princes, the supreme commanders, the rich and the poor, and even the noble Envoys, and you find that death has left none of them untouched. Then you will be sure that death is your inevitable end, despite all efforts, just as it was the end of those who came before you. There is no escape and no way to get away from it. At that time, you will find no hope in this life and you will know that it is no more than a temporary world.

Thinking of death produces fear and awe in your spirit, and generates a serious desire to attain knowledge of the Provider, making you truly rush to seek Him. You ask yourself Who this Provider is, Who created you from semen

-

though you were nothing worth mentioning before this

-

and then made you into a child and then a perfect person. You contemplate the universe once again, but you look deeper than before. There you will find that It is this Provider Who steers the sun and the moon and directs all of the universe and all of its contents in order to provide for you and to fulfill all your demands and meet all your needs. There is no hand and no act of anyone besides Him. He alone is Al’lah, apart from whom there is no god.

Hence, you will move from believing in the Provider to new level, which is belief in this Provider as the Steering God. You will see the heavenly bodies swimming within their orbits, and witness the sun sending down its rays and heat. Moreover, you will see the clouds moving, stirred from their hidden sites, and the winds running violently according to their directions. You will see the waters of the large seas scrambling and their waves chopping, the rivers flowing down from their sources, running to their mouths where they enter the seas. As for the terrestrial globe, you will see it swimming within its space and its orbit, circulating around itself, along with all the creatures it carries on its surface. You will see all of this moving, but only through God’s Power and Command. You will think more and more deeply until you realize that no creature can take a single step or raise a hand or move a single inch except by God’s Leave, Will, and Power.

Thence you will advance in thinking, rising and ascending until you reach a degree of understanding where you witness that the whole universe is but a single unit of connected parts and bonded atoms. Furthermore, you will recognize that it all works in harmony and uniformity, and that the Godly Will watches over it and supports it. Thus, the Provider is the Steering God of the whole universe, and there is no director or god other than He.

You will know that your Provider is Al’lah, and therefore, having witnessed this in the universe with your spirit and ascertained it in your own depths, you will say with your tongue that there is no god but Al’lah. You will utter it with your tongue because it is lodged in your mind; you will not be dependent on imitation or what you have heard from others. Your belief in this will be akin to the belief of the goodly ancestors and the noble companions rather than the belief of old men, which is based on legends and illusions. Thus, you will attain true belief in this statement and will actually say: “There is no god except Al’lah”. That is some of what we understand of God’s Saying:

“Know that there is no god but Al’lah…”

385

In the noble saying, the Envoy (cpth) says:

“He who says, ‘There is no god but Al’lah’, faithfully and loyally, will enter Paradise. It was said: ‘What is the sign of its loyalty?’ He said: ‘To keep him away from what is forbidden by Al’lah’.”

386

Surely, this will prevent anyone from committing the deeds forbidden by God, because they will see that Al’lah the Almighty is with them, watching and observing them wherever they turn and whatever they do.

§§§§§

Having arrived at this stage

-

the belief that there is no god but Al’lah, and the belief in the Provider

-

I will advance quickly, since you are now able to accompany me without delay. I now want to reveal to you the effects of the belief that there is no god but Al’lah, and to lead you to the love of the Envoy of God (cpth). Therefore, I say that when you believe that there is no god but Al’lah you become one of those who sees that God’s Hand controls the movement of the universe. When your spirit is immersed in this view you will witness that no winds blow, no clouds cover the sky or stick together, no rains flow, no lightning flashes or shimmers, no thunder resounds, no sea runs high or low with restless waves, no river water flows in constant flux, no volcano breaks out angrily, no flood streams forth with force or intensity, no earthquake shakes the land and makes forgetful and heedless hearts tremble in fear, no earth rotates, causing night and day and the four seasons, no stars swim shining within the system of their orbits, except as directed by the Hand of the Wise and Peerless One. That is to say, according to your efforts and your daily contemplations, you will witness that the universe

-

with all its creatures

-

is but one unit steered by the Will of the Cognizant and Omniscient One. What is more, without Him your hand does not move, your eye does not blink, your ear does not hear a sound or a noise, your heart does not beat its pulses between systole and diastole, your stomach does not secrete its gastric juice over the foods inside it, your liver does not store substances or secrete others according to its firm standards, your lungs do not expand and contract between inhalation and expiration, your blood does not flow in arteries and veins, the red corpuscles do not carry what they carry to and fro, the white corpuscles do not fight and struggle with microbes, and germs do not severely attack the body. Furthermore, I say that if you become sure of all this by way of thought and spiritual witnessing, rather than by listening to specialists or reading volumes and books, you will see that everything is controlled by God’s Hand and that all people, be they notables or commoners, be they near or far, be they strong or weak, and even all of the creatures of the earth

-

none of these can render you any benefit, nor protect you from any evil, nor hurt you, nor cause any change in your situation, except by Al’lah’s Leave. Thus you will enter the fort of straightness, and you will never exceed God’s bounds. Since the spirit cannot remain motionless, you will find that once it has forsaken misdeeds and turned wholly towards Al’lah, it will spare no effort in doing charity and favor. It will become engaged in helping everyone in need, because it will wish to approach Al’lah by means of this activity.

At this stage

-

the stage of straightness upon God’s Order and approaching Him by doing favor

-

the spirit will be confident of its charity and of God’s Satisfaction with it. As a result of such confidence, it will draw nearer to its Creator and turn wholly towards Him, so that a link will be established. Then its communication with God will be correct. It will see that it lives in a state of proximity rather than distance, feeling love and purity rather than coolness or disinclination. It will consequently enjoy a happy life of repose and bliss. At this time, the spirit will gain two fruits that it would never have gained without this link to the Creator and the entrance into His Presence, and it will gain them only by virtue of this link, this direction, and this pleasant communication with God.

The first fruit

is that

-

by turning towards its Creator

-

all sins will fall away from the spirit, with the word ‘sins’ here referring to the mean desires that are attached to the spirit and the defects that are rooted in it. Thus, by communicating with God, these lowly yearnings will be eroded, dropping away so that the spirit will be pure of disease. It will emerge from this communication having acquired purification and cleanliness; it will be free of the lust that once disturbed it and the dirt that once befouled it. There will be no stinginess, no cowardice, no attachment to this worldly life, no miserliness, no rudeness, no grossness, no hard-heartedness, no desire to do damage, no cowering, no subservience, no inclination to oppression or aggression, and no wish for worldly glory or authority. Thus, there will be none of the bad qualities that degrade humanity’s esteem or standing among people or with God.

All of these negative qualities will be wiped out by the link with Al’lah and the entrance into His Presence. The Envoy (cpth) explained the effect that communication with God has on the spirit of humanity in a noble saying, where he (cpth) says:

“Suppose there is a river flowing beside the doorway of one of you, and that this person washes himself there, five times a day. What do you say about this? Will any of his dirt remain? They said that no dirt would remain. He told them that this example explains the five prayers. Al’lah effaces misdeeds through them.”

387

That is the first fruit that results from entering into God’s Presence and performing the correct communication.

As for the second fruit

, here it is explained, and how delighted you will be if you get it! When your spirit attains the link with your Creator, you will feel life flowing in its depths, just as one feels the reviving warmth of the sun in days of bitter coldness. You will feel life spreading in your spirit, as one feels a breeze of fresh and gentle air while sitting in the shadow of a tree on a midsummer’s day. You will feel life entering your spirit, just as a thirsty person feels cool water flowing into their body, quenching their thirst and refreshing their body and soul. You will feel so much, and there is not feeling of the believer more beautiful than what they feel in the times of their closeness to their Creator and Provider.

Moreover, while you are absorbed in this state of lofty and sublime feeling, high impressions of perfection will be imprinted on the surface of your spirit. That is the second fruit that the spirit gains through true communication and nearness to Al’lah. This perfection, which colors the spirit at the time of its entrance into God’s Presence, will be manifested in the spirit of the believer in the form of mercy, tenderness, generosity, bounty, chivalry, helping the needy, telling the truth, openness of speech, kindness, gentleness, politeness, patience, deliberateness, modesty, bravery, justice, equity, self-esteem, a sense of honor, resistance to falseness, and so forth.

Whatever attributes and indications of perfection you may mention, you will find that the spirit acquires them and is colored by them when it is near to Al’lah, for God says:

“It is the stain of Al’lah. And who gives a better stain than Al’lah? And we are worshiping Him.”

388

§§§§§

When the spirit reaches such a stage and ascends to such a rank through its perfection and high manners, you will find that it loves all people of perfection and high merit. It will love every perfect person because of the perfection it has achieved itself, for none appreciates a favor except those who possess it, and only people of perfection can know perfection. In this way, if the spirit sees people of generosity and bounty, it appreciates their advances over itself in generosity and bounty, and if it meets people of compassion and affection, it esteems their superiority over itself in compassion and affection. So it is with all the other supreme qualities and morals. The spirit will appreciate any who surpasses and exceeds it. Therefore it will love perfect believers when it finds them, and if it meets truthful leaders it will adore them and accompany them. The Envoy of God (cpth) is the master of the people of perfection, and supersedes all the worlds in this domain. Moreover, because of his closeness to his Creator, he (cpth) attained the greatest share of perfection from that Godly Presence, so that no angel or human could approach his rank. Consequently, you will find that a believer reveres God’s Envoy (cpth) whole-heartedly.

In the view of a believer, there is no creature greater than the Envoy, and nobody has a rank loftier than his (cpth). When believers hear something about him (cpth), their hearts long for him; if his name or his merits or his deeds are mentioned, their spirits travel over large distances and set aside the eras and generations that separate them, arriving to join and accompany that venerable spirit, maintaining a firm link with it that never breaks or sunders.

By way of this spiritual flowing, and through this moral connection, in the company of that spirit

-

that is, the pure and virtuous spirit of the Envoy (cpth)

-

and by becoming one of those who reach such a level, your spirit will ascend gently and without feeling in the company of the Envoy’s spirit, which is always entering into Al’lah. Thus your spirit will be together with that of the Envoy (cpth) in God’s Presence.

At that moment, the light of the Envoy (cpth)

-

whom Almighty Al’lah has called ‘the shining lamp’

-

will illuminate an aspect of God’s Perfection for you. This will allow you to witness what you deserve of God’s Compassion, Tenderness, Sympathy, Kindness, Clemency, Charity, Justice, Might, Knowledge, Wisdom, abundant Favor, Provision, comprehensive Steering, Boons for every being that has life and a soul, and all the other Godly Attributes, which no one can witness without becoming infatuated with them and adoring them.

Out of its passion and love for the Godly Perfection that arises from seeing the Supreme Attributes, the spirit attains a high link with its Creator. This link is achieved through the love that is produced when one witnesses the Godly Attributes and Perfection. Furthermore, through this link the spirit will acquire a light from Al’lah the Almighty that allows it to see goodness, and understand that it really is good. Consequently, the spirit likes and inclines towards this goodness. Similarly, the spirit comes to see evil and understand that it really is evil, and so it disdains and loathes this evil.

By my life, this is the piety (seeing by Al’lah’s Light) to which the Almighty Al’lah urged His believing worshipers, and with which He charged them.

“You, who

(certainly)

believe! See by Al’lah’s Light, and be with the truthful.”

389

God says:

“You who believe; see by Al’lah’s Light and believe in His Envoy. He will grant you two portions of His Compassion and make a light for you by which you can go, and forgive you: Al’lah is Forgiving and Merciful.”

390

In another Fortress He says:

“You who believe; if you become illuminated by Al’lah’s Light, He will grant you discernment and cleanse you of your sins and forgive you. Al’lah is of great bounty.”

391

He also says:

“You who believe; see by Al’lah’s Light and speak apposite speech. He will make your works right and forgive you your sins. Those who obey Al’lah and His Envoy shall win a great victory.”

392

Undoubtedly, that is piety in its reality. In Arabic, the word ‘piety’ means ‘avoidance.’ Therefore we can understand that ‘piety’ means avoiding evil through Al’lah’s Light. This is the avoidance of danger, having witnessed the causes of corruption in this worldly life by means of the Godly Light

-

the Light which you would never have gained access to, if your spirit had not connected with that of the Envoy (cpth).

Thus belief in the Envoy (cpth) comes after belief in God, and loving the Envoy (cpth) is always joined with the right faith and associated with true communication with God. The noble saying denotes:

“He that has no love has no faith. He that has no love has no faith. He that has no love has no faith.”

Indeed, the favor of the Envoy is so limitless that none can express it.

Conclusion

In our next publication we will present a study of the Companions of the Cave: how they abandoned worldly pleasures, despite being the sons of the ministers and notables of their people, and despite still being in the prime of youth and vitality. We discuss how they made full use of their thinking and were therefore shocked to see how their people were immersed in love for this world and idolatry. They did not then remain in step with these people, but preferred to refuse the bitter reality of their lives, earnestly and seriously turning to look for their Creator, seeking to recognize the reason behind their own existence. These youths pondered their own creation and the creation of the heavens and the earth, until they fully realized God’s Existence by witnessing and viewing with the eye of spirit. Thus they were protected by this faith, and later became ideal and high examples in the method of thinking, providing a demonstration of how to acquire true faith for humanity throughout the ages.

However, the question is:

Is there any relationship between the Companions of the Cave and Jesus Christ (pth)? Does their appearance depend on his (pth)?

In non-Arabic languages, those young men are called ‘the Sleepers of the Cave.’ There is no doubt that there must be a time when a sleeper gets up

-

is this not so?

Is their waking connected to the waking of our master Jesus and his mother (peace is through both of them)?

Are they still alive, despite this long period of time having passed? Is it true that they did not die, but that God only put off their appearance by letting them surrender to sleep?!

Where are the Companions of the Cave sleeping? Which country are they in, and in which Cave?

Why did they sleep?! What is their true story?! If they died, as some people claim, then why does God engage our minds with their story? What is the purpose of mentioning their story in the Holy heavenly Books?

The answers to these questions will play a part in our discussion of the second coming of Jesus Christ in our new book.

A Glimpse of the Life of the Eminent Scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (His soul has been sanctified by Al’lah)

“Have you not heard how Al’lah dealt with the ‘Ad, the people of Irama, the many-columned, most important city, whose like has never been created in the land; also with the Thamoud, who brought rocks through the valley; as well as with Pharaoh, the owner of the stakes? They all exceeded human limits and made the lands teem with corruption. Therefore, your Provider let loose a scourge of punishment upon them, for your Provider observes all.”

These noble verses reveal that the corruption of that era was a result of the huge deluxe constructions which they built. The ‘Ad continued to extend their city until it became the most beautiful place in the world at that time. So it was with the Thamoud, who brought rocks from the mountains to their city in order to establish palaces therein. The rocks were carried on planks or in ships that were specially prepared for that purpose, and were driven by the water flowing in the ravines. The Pharaonic people also used the Nile Valley to transfer rocks from the south in order to build the pyramids. The Almighty God has likened these pyramids to the mountains, and described them both with the word ‘stakes.’ Those same people also constructed temples and castles, among many other things. These works and the ensuing ornamentation and debauchery caused immorality and envy in people’s hearts. Thus, society became divided into an opulent class and a class of abject poverty, who suffered privation and misery. Consequently, dissension prevailed and humanity vanished; that was when your Provider let loose a scourge of torment upon them.
